title: Preparation & Intention
description: Standing position, direction of gaze, foot position, and intention.

items.title: Standing is a Pillar
items.description: Standing during obligatory prayer is a pillar of prayer. Prayer becomes invalid if abandoned by those who are able...
items.content_markdown:
### Standing is a Pillar

Standing during obligatory prayer is a pillar of prayer. Prayer becomes invalid if abandoned by those who are able. The evidence is the Prophet's ﷺ words to a companion who did not yet understand how to pray:

> **إِذَا قُمْتَ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ فَأَسْبِغِ الْوُضُوءَ، ثُمَّ اسْتَقْبِلِ الْقِبْلَةَ فَكَبِّرْ**
>
> "When you stand for prayer, perform ablution completely, then face the qiblah and say takbir..."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 757, Muslim 397)*

If unable to stand, one may sit. If unable to sit, one may lie down.

> **صَلِّ قَائِمًا، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ فَقَاعِدًا، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ فَعَلَى جَنْبٍ**
>
> "Pray standing, if you cannot then sitting, if you cannot then lying on your side"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 1117)*

items.title: Direction of Gaze
items.description: It is recommended to look toward the place of prostration for greater khushu', although there is no explicit evidence...
items.content_markdown:
### Direction of Gaze

It is recommended to look toward the place of prostration for greater khushu' (concentration), although there is no *sharih* (explicit) evidence. However, it is strongly prohibited to look upward (at the ceiling) or to turn one's head without need.

**Prohibition of looking upward:**
> **لَيَنْتَهِيَنَّ أَقْوَامٌ يَرْفَعُونَ أَبْصَارَهُمْ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فِى الصَّلاَةِ أَوْ لاَ تَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ**
>
> "Let those people who raise their eyes toward the sky during prayer stop doing so, or their sight will not return to them"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 750, Muslim 428)*

**Prohibition of turning (without need):**
> **هُوَ اخْتِلاسٌ يَخْتَلِسُهُ الشَّيْطَانُ مِنْ صَلَاةِ الْعَبْدِ**
>
> "It is a snatching that Satan snatches from a servant's prayer"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 751)*

items.title: Foot Position
items.description: It is sunnah to space the feet moderately (not too wide, not too close). Touching feet with the person next to you...
items.content_markdown:
### Foot Position

It is sunnah to space the feet moderately (not too wide, not too close). Touching feet with the person next to you is done during congregational prayer to straighten the rows.

> **أَقِيمُوا صُفُوفَكُمْ وَتَرَاصُّوا، فَإِنِّي أَرَاكُمْ مِنْ وَرَاءِ ظَهْرِي**
>
> "Straighten your rows and stand close together, for I see you from behind my back"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 719)*

Companion Anas bin Malik said: *"Each of us would touch his shoulder with his companion's shoulder and his foot with his companion's foot."* (Narrated by Bukhari 725).

items.title: Intention is in the Heart
items.description: Scholars unanimously agree that the place of intention is in the heart. Intention is the desire (al-qasdu) to perform...
items.content_markdown:
### Intention is in the Heart

Scholars unanimously agree that the place of intention is in the heart. Intention is the desire (al-qasdu) to perform prayer. A person who stands facing the qiblah to pray Dhuhr has already made the intention.

> **إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى**
>
> "Actions are but by intentions, and every person will have what they intended."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 1, Muslim 1907)*

items.title: Ruling on Verbalizing Intention (Ushalli)
items.description: Loudly reciting the intention (such as Ushalli fardhol...) is neither obligatory nor sunnah according to scholarly consensus...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Verbalizing Intention (Ushalli)

Loudly reciting the intention (such as *Ushalli fardhol...*) is neither obligatory nor sunnah according to scholarly consensus. There is no narration from the Prophet ﷺ or the companions verbalizing intention before takbir.

The Prophet ﷺ began prayer directly with Takbir:
> **كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَسْتَفْتِحُ الصَّلاةَ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to begin prayer with takbir"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 498)*

Ibn Qayyim said: *"The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never said 'ushalli lillah...' nor verbalized intention. This is bid'ah. There is not a single authentic or even weak narration from the Prophet ﷺ or companions about this."* (Zaadul Ma'ad, 1/201).

Some Shafi'i scholars who permit "verbalizing" mean it as a means to help the heart (wasilah), not believing it to be a specifically taught sunnah of the Prophet. However, what is more virtuous and safe from whispers is to suffice with intention in the heart coinciding with Takbiratul Ihram.

title: Takbiratul Ihram
description: Complete guide to Takbiratul Ihram according to sunnah.

items.title: Can Allahu Akbar be Replaced?
items.description: Replacing the takbiratul ihram wording, for example with الله أجلُّ /Allahu Ajall/ or الله أعظمُ /Allahu A'zham/ or other phrases...
items.content_markdown:
### Can Allahu Akbar be Replaced?

Replacing the takbiratul ihram wording, for example with الله أجلُّ /Allahu Ajall/ or الله أعظمُ /Allahu A'zham/ or other phrases, is haram (forbidden), even if they are still phrases of praise and glorification of Allah. This is because the takbir wording is tauqifiyyah (established by evidence). Replacing it with other phrases is bid'ah (innovation).

However, scholars differ regarding using الله الأكبرُ /Allahul Akbar/ (with alif lam). Some scholars, such as Imam Abu Hanifah and Imam Ash Shafi'i, consider it valid. Imam Shafi'i stated that the alif lam in this phrase is merely an addition that does not change the wording or meaning (Shifatu Shalatin Nabi, 58). Similarly regarding replacing Allahu Akbar with non-Arabic language.

**The Correct View:**

All of this contradicts the sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ. It is not permissible to replace the takbir wording with anything other than الله أكبرُ. This is because the hadiths mentioning the takbir wording in prayer only mention الله أكبرُ. For example:

> **إنَّهُ لا تتمُّ صلاةٌ لأحدٍ منَ النَّاسِ حتَّى يتوضَّأَ فيضعَ الوضوءَ مواضعَهُ ثمَّ يقولُ اللَّهُ أَكبرُ**
>
> "No one's prayer is complete until they perform ablution, placing water in its proper places, then say 'Allahu Akbar'"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 857, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Abi Daud)*

And the Prophet ﷺ said:

> **صلوا كما رأيتُموني أصلي**
>
> "Pray as you have seen me pray"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 631, 5615, 6008)*

**For Non-Arabs:**

For non-Arabs who have difficulty or cannot pronounce takbir, some scholars such as the Shafi'iyyah, Hanabilah, and Abu Yusuf permit pronouncing takbir in another language. Some scholars such as the Malikiyyah and Al Qadhi Abu Ya'la hold that the obligation of takbiratul ihram is waived for them.

items.title: Volume of Takbir
items.description: Takbiratul ihram must be pronounced with the tongue, not merely in the heart. Scholars then differ on whether the minimum volume...
items.content_markdown:
### Volume of Takbir

Takbiratul ihram must be pronounced with the tongue, not merely in the heart. Scholars then differ on whether the minimum volume must be audible to oneself or not. Some scholars such as the Hanabilah require this, meaning the takbir sound must be audible to the person next to them or at least to the speaker themselves (Syarhul Mumthi', 3/20).

**The Correct View:**

However, the more correct opinion is that this is not required. Shaykh Al Utsaimin said: "The correct view is that it is not required for a person to hear their own takbir. This is because hearing the takbir is zaaid (external) to the pronunciation itself. Therefore, whoever claims this is obligatory must bring evidence" (Syarhul Mumthi', 3/20).

items.title: How Does a Mute Person Say Takbir?
items.description: A mute person or someone with a physical disability preventing speech may say takbir in their heart...
items.content_markdown:
### How Does a Mute Person Say Takbir?

A mute person or someone with a physical disability preventing speech may say takbir in their heart. Shaykh Muhammad bin Shalih Al Utsaimin explained: "Because saying Allahu Akbar encompasses both verbal speech and heart speech. A person's tongue does not say Allahu Akbar except that their heart certainly says it and intends it. Therefore, if someone is prevented from verbalizing it, what is obligatory for them is to suffice with saying it in their heart" (Syarhul Mumthi', 3/20).

**Moving the Lips:**

However, scholars differ on whether such a person must move their lips while saying it in their heart. Some scholars such as the Shafi'iyyah still require moving the lips, because what is called "al qaul" in Arabic is accompanied by lip movement. And if someone is prevented from saying takbir completely, they must say takbir according to their ability, including moving their lips.

Some scholars such as the Malikiyyah, Hanabilah, and Hanafiyyah do not require this, because lip movement is not the goal but rather a means or wasilah for pronouncing takbir. Therefore, when someone is prevented from pronunciation, the means also falls away. And mere lip movement is not considered in shari'ah (Syarhul Mumthi', 3/20, Mausu'ah Fiqhiyyah Kuwaitiyyah, 19/92).

items.title: Raising Both Hands
items.description: Scholars unanimously agree that raising both hands during takbiratul ihram is legislated. The evidence is the hadith...
items.content_markdown:
### Raising Both Hands

Scholars unanimously agree that raising both hands during takbiratul ihram is legislated. The evidence is the hadith:

> **أنَّ النبيَّ صلّى الله عليه وسلّم كان يرفعُ يديه حذوَ مَنكبيه؛ إذا افتتح الصَّلاةَ، وإذا كبَّرَ للرُّكوع، وإذا رفع رأسه من الرُّكوع**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ used to raise his hands level with his shoulders when beginning prayer, when saying takbir for ruku, and when raising his head from ruku"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 735)*

**Ruling - Obligatory or Sunnah?**

However, they differ regarding its ruling. Some scholars say it is obligatory, such as Al Auza'i, Al Humaidi, Ibn Khuzaimah, and Al Hakim. Their evidence is that the hadiths show the Prophet ﷺ always raised his hands during takbiratul ihram. And he said:

> **صلوا كما رأيتُموني أصلي**
>
> "Pray as you have seen me pray"

However, this opinion is not correct, because many prayer procedures that he always performed such as sitting tawarruk, sitting iftirasy, reciting the opening supplication, etc. are not obligatory. In fact, these are not considered obligatory even by the scholars who require raising hands during takbiratul ihram. Therefore, there is idthirad (inconsistency) in this opinion.

**The Correct View:**

The correct view is that Ibnul Mundzir has transmitted scholarly consensus (ijma) that raising hands during takbiratul ihram is sunnah (Shifatu Shalatin Nabi, 63-67).

items.title: Form of Fingers and Palms
items.description: Fingers should be spread apart, neither too open nor pressed together. Based on the hadith...
items.content_markdown:
### Form of Fingers and Palms

**Fingers:**

Fingers should be spread apart, neither too open nor pressed together. Based on the hadith:

> **كان إذا قام إلى الصلاة قال هكذا – وأشار أبو عامر بيده ولم يفرج بين أصابعه ولم يضمها**
>
> "When the Prophet ﷺ prayed, he did like this - Abu Amir (the narrator) gestured with his hand, he neither spread his fingers apart nor pressed them together"
> *(Narrated by Ibn Khuzaimah 459, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Ibn Khuzaimah)*

**Palms:**

Regarding the palms, some scholars such as Ibnul Qayyim, At Thahawi, Abu Yusuf, and most Hanabilah recommend directing the palms straight toward the qiblah when raising both hands, using as evidence the hadith:

> **إذا استفتح أحدُكم الصلاةَ فليرفع يديْهِ ، وليستقبل بباطنِهما القِبلةَ**
>
> "When one of you begins prayer, let them raise their hands and face their palms toward the qiblah"
> *(Narrated by Al Baihaqi in Sunan Al Kubra 2/27, in Silsilah Adh Dha'ifah (2338) Al Albani said: "very weak")*

There are several hadiths with similar meaning but none are authentic. As for the hadith from Wa'il bin Hujr:

> **لأنظرن الى صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه و سلم قال فلما افتتح الصلاة كبر ورفع يديه فرأيت إبهاميه قريبا من أذنيه**
>
> "I truly observed the Prophet's ﷺ prayer. When he began prayer, he said takbir and raised his hands until I saw his thumbs near his ears"
> *(Narrated by An Nasa'i 1101, authenticated by Al Albani in Sunan An Nasa'i)*

This is not explicit evidence for this practice. However, there is an authentic athar from Ibn Umar:

> **انه كان اذا كبر استحب ان يستقبل بإبهامه القبلة**
>
> "Ibn Umar used to like to face his thumbs toward the qiblah when saying takbir"
> *(Narrated by Ibn Sa'd in Ath Thabaqat 4/157, quoted from Shifatu Shalatin Nabi, 63)*

**The Correct View:**

The correct view, inshaAllah, is that directing the palms toward the qiblah during takbiratul ihram is permissible as Ibn Umar did, but it is not sunnah (Shifatu Shalatin Nabi, 63-66).

items.title: Height Measurement
items.description: Both hands are raised to shoulder level or to ear level. Based on the hadiths...
items.content_markdown:
### Height Measurement

Both hands are raised to shoulder level or to ear level. Based on the hadiths:

> **كان رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلمَ إذا قام إلى الصلاةِ يرفعُ يديه حذوَ مِنكَبيه**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise his hands to shoulder level when praying"
> *(Narrated by Ahmad 9/28, Ahmad Syakir said: "the chain of this hadith is authentic")*

Also:

> **كانَ رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم إذا افتتحَ الصلاةَ رفعَ يدَيهِ حتى تكوناَ حَذْوَ أُذُنَيهِ**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise his hands to ear level when beginning prayer"
> *(Narrated by Al Baihaqi 2/26)*

Also from Malik bin Huwairits:

> **أنه رأى نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم . وقال : حتى يحاذي بهما فروع أذنيه**
>
> "He saw the Prophet ﷺ pray, he said: (his hands were raised) to the level of his earlobes"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 391, Abu Daud 745)*

**Khilaf Tanawwu' (Variation in Practice):**

This is khilaf tanawwu' (difference in variation), so a person may choose any of the available methods. In fact, it is more virtuous to sometimes practice one method and sometimes another, so that each of these sunnahs remains alive and practiced.

Some scholars specify these measurements, meaning the bottom of the palm at shoulder level, or the top of the palm at earlobe level. However, the correct view is that the matter is broad in this regard. Raising the palms to around the shoulders or around the ears without specific limits already fulfills what the Prophet made sunnah (see Syarhul Mumthi, 3/31).

As for the practice of some people who believe the palms must touch the earlobes, this has no basis whatsoever (Shifatu Shalatin Nabi, 63).

items.title: Takbir First or Raise Hands First?
items.description: According to Malikiyyah and Shafi'iyyah, takbir is simultaneous with raising hands. According to Hanafiyyah and one Shafi'i opinion...
items.content_markdown:
### Takbir First or Raise Hands First?

According to Malikiyyah and Shafi'iyyah, takbir is simultaneous with raising hands. According to Hanafiyyah and one Shafi'i opinion, raising hands is before takbir. Some Hanafi scholars also hold that raising hands is after takbir.

**The Correct View:**

The correct view is that this matter can be tolerated, meaning it is permissible to raise hands before takbir, after takbir, or simultaneously with takbir. This is because all of these were practiced by the Prophet ﷺ (Ashlu Sifati Shalatin Nabi, 193-199).

**Evidence for Before Takbir:**

Hadith from Ibn Umar:

> **كان رسول الله صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إذا قام إلى الصلاة؛ رفع يديه حتى تكونا حذو منكبيه ثم كبَّر**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise his hands to shoulder level, then say takbir"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 390)*

Hadith from Abu Humaid As Sa'idi:

> **كان رسول الله صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إذا قام إلى الصلاة؛ يرفع يديه حتى يحاذي بهما منكبيه، ثم يكبر**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise his hands to shoulder level, then say takbir"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 729, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Abi Daud)*

**Evidence for Simultaneous:**

Hadith from Ibn Umar:

> **رأيت النبي صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ افتتح التكبير في الصلاة، فرفع يديه حين يكبر حتى يجعلهما حذو منكبيه، وإذا كبَّر للركوع؛ فعل مثله**
>
> "I saw the Prophet ﷺ begin prayer with takbir. He raised his hands when saying takbir to shoulder level. When he said takbir for ruku, he did likewise"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 738)*

Hadith from Malik Ibnul Huwairits:

> **أن رسول الله كان إذا صلى ، يرفع يديه حين يكبر حذو أذنيه ، وإذا أراد أن يركع ، وإذا رفع رأسه من الركوع**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise his hands when saying takbir to ear level. He did this when intending to perform ruku and when raising his head from ruku"
> *(Narrated by An Nasa'i 879, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Sunan Nasa'i)*

**Evidence for After Takbir:**

Hadith from Abu Qilabah:

> **أنه رأى مالك بن الحويرث ، إذا صلى كبر . ثم رفع يديه . وإذا أراد أن يركع رفع يديه . وإذا رفع رأسه من الركوع رفع يديه . وحدث ؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يفعل هكذا**
>
> "He saw Malik bin Al Huwairits say takbir when praying, then raise his hands. When he intended to perform ruku, he also raised his hands. When he raised his head from ruku, he also raised his hands. And he said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also did this"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 391)*

items.title: Ruling on Placing Hands
items.description: Scholars unanimously agree that placing hands during prayer is legislated, based on the hadith from Sahl bin Sa'ad...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Placing Hands

Scholars unanimously agree that placing hands during prayer is legislated, based on the hadith from Sahl bin Sa'ad:

> **كان الناسُ يؤمَرون أن يضَع الرجلُ اليدَ اليُمنى على ذِراعِه اليُسرى في الصلاةِ**
>
> "People used to be commanded to place the right hand on the left forearm during prayer"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari 740)*

**Imam Malik's Opinion:**

Some have transmitted from Imam Malik that he considered placing hands (bersedekap) makruh in prayer and recommended irsal, which is letting the hands hang at the sides. However, what is authentic is that he also held the view that placing hands is legislated. The evidence is in Al Muwatha, where he made a chapter titled:

*Chapter: Placing Both Hands, One on Top of the Other, During Prayer*

**Sunnah, Not Obligatory:**

Although the Bukhari hadith contains the command to place hands, no statement is known from the salaf, whether from companions, tabi'in, tabi'ut tabi'in, or the imams of madhhabs, stating that placing hands in prayer is obligatory (see Sifat Shalat Nabi Lit Tharifi, 84). Therefore, placing hands in prayer is sunnah, not obligatory.

items.title: Form of Placement
items.description: Scholars unanimously agree that the right hand is on top of the left hand, but they differ regarding the detailed form...
items.content_markdown:
### Form of Placement

Scholars unanimously agree that the right hand is on top of the left hand, but they differ regarding the detailed form of placement, which is khilaf tanawwu' (difference in variation). Nevertheless, the correct ways of placing hands are divided into two methods:

**1. Al Wadh'u (Placing right on left without encircling or grasping)**

The right hand is placed in three locations: on the back of the left hand, on the left wrist, and on the left forearm. The evidence is the hadith from Wa'il bin Hujr about the Prophet's prayer:

> **ثم وضَع يدَه اليُمنى على ظهرِ كفِّه اليُسرى والرُّسغِ والساعدِ**
>
> "...then he placed his right hand on the back of his left palm, or on the wrist, or on the forearm"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 727, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Abi Daud)*

In the Maliki and Hanbali madhhabs, they recommend placing the right hand on the back of the left palm. In the Shafi'i madhhab, the right hand is placed on the back of the left palm, on the left wrist, and on part of the forearm.

**2. Al Qabdhu (Right hand fingers encircling or grasping the left hand)**

The evidence is the hadith from Wa'il bin Hujr:

> **رأيتُ رسولَ اللَّهِ إذا كانَ قائمًا في الصَّلاةِ قبضَ بيمينِهِ على شمالِهِ**
>
> "I saw the Prophet ﷺ standing in prayer, grasping his left hand with his right hand"
> *(Narrated by An Nasa'i 886, Al Baihaqi 2/28, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih An Nasa'i)*

**Incorrect Methods:**

As for methods outside these two, such as placing the right hand on the left elbow or on the upper arm, this is an error and no scholar permits it.

Shaykh Muhammad bin Shalih Al Utsaimin said: "We have seen people placing hands by holding their elbows. Does this have a basis? The answer is, this has no basis whatsoever" (Syarhul Mumthi', 3/36).

**Men and Women:**

Some scholars differentiate between men's and women's methods of placing hands, but the correct view is that the method for men and women is the same. This is because originally the worship procedures exemplified by the Prophet apply to both men and women unless there is evidence differentiating them.

items.title: Location of Placement
items.description: Scholars differ regarding the location of hand placement. Hanafi and Hanbali madhhabs: hold that the location is below the navel...
items.content_markdown:
### Location of Placement

Scholars differ regarding the location of hand placement.

**Hanafi and Hanbali Madhhabs:** hold that the location is below the navel. Based on a hadith from Ali (but this hadith is very weak).

**Shafi'iyyah and Malikiyyah:** hold that it is below the chest and above the navel. Their evidence is the hadith of Wa'il bin Hujr:

> **كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَضَعُ يَدَهُ الْيُمْنَى عَلَى يَدِهِ الْيُسْرَى ثُمَّ يَشُدُّ بَيْنَهُمَا عَلَى صَدْرِهِ وَهُوَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to place his right hand on his left hand, then tighten them on his chest while praying"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 759)*

However, the correct view is that this hadith is weak.

**The Correct View: No Specific Limit (Matter is Broad)**

It is also transmitted as one of Imam Ahmad's opinions that the location of hand placement is precisely on the chest, according to the apparent meaning of the hadith. This is also strengthened by Shaykh Muhammad bin Shalih Al Utsaimin and Shaykh Al Albani rahimahumallah.

However, since there is no authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ about this, the correct view is that there is no specific limit for hand placement location. In this matter, the ruling is broad. Placing hands is permissible on the chest, below the chest, on the stomach, above the navel, or below the navel.

**Incorrect Practice:**

As for placing hands on the left chest or left ribs (heart), this is a fabricated reason with no basis. Additionally, there is a hadith from Abu Hurairah:

> **نهى أن يصلي الرجل مختصرا**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ forbade a person from praying with hands on hips"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 1220, Muslim 545)*

items.content_markdown:
### Placing Hands After Ruku

Some salaf scholars recommend placing hands after rising from ruku, including Al Qadhi Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hazm, and Al Kasani. They use as evidence the hadith of Wa'il bin Hujr:

> **"I saw the Prophet ﷺ standing in prayer, grasping his left hand with his right hand"**

The phrase *"when he was standing in prayer"* is understood to mean that placing hands is done in every standing position in prayer, whether before ruku or after ruku.

**The Correct View:**

However, this is not explicit evidence. Since there is no authentic and explicit hadith about this, the scholarly difference in this matter is ijtihadi difference, and the matter is broad. Imam Ahmad said: *"I hope this matter is not made narrow."*

items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Reciting Opening Supplication

The ruling is sunnah (recommended). Among the evidence is the hadith from Abu Hurairah:

> **كان رسول الله صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إذا كبَّر في الصلاة؛ سكتَ هُنَيَّة قبل أن يقرأ. فقلت: يا رسول الله! بأبي أنت وأمي؛ أرأيت سكوتك بين التكبير والقراءة؛ ما تقول؟ قال: " أقول: … " فذكره**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, after saying takbir in prayer, would pause briefly before reciting. I asked: 'O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be ransomed for you, what do you say during your pause between takbir and recitation?' He said: 'I say:...' (then he mentioned the opening supplication)"
> *(Muttafaqun 'alaih - Agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim)*

After mentioning several opening supplications in his book Al-Adhkar, Imam An-Nawawi said: "Know that all these supplications are mustahabbah (recommended) in both obligatory and voluntary prayers" (Al-Adhkar, 1/107).

This is the opinion of the majority of scholars, except for Imam Malik rahimahullah. He held the opinion that what is recited after takbiratul ihram is **الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العَالَمِينَ** (Al-Fatihah directly). Of course, his opinion is not correct as it contradicts many evidences.

items.content_markdown:
### 1. First Supplication

> **اللَّهُمَّ بَاعِدْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ خَطَايَايَ، كَمَا بَاعَدْتَ بَيْنَ المَشْرِقِ وَالمَغْرِبِ، اللَّهُمَّ نَقِّنِي مِنَ الخَطَايَا كَمَا يُنَقَّى الثَّوْبُ الأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الدَّنَسِ، اللَّهُمَّ اغْسِلْ خَطَايَايَ بِالْمَاءِ وَالثَّلْجِ وَالبَرَدِ**

"O Allah, distance me from my sins as You have distanced the East from the West. O Allah, cleanse me from sins as white cloth is cleansed from dirt. O Allah, wash my sins with water, snow, and ice."
*(Narrated by Bukhari 2/182, Muslim 2/98)*

The Prophet ﷺ used to recite this supplication in obligatory prayers. This supplication is the most authentic among the opening supplications, as stated by Ibn Hajar in Fathul Bari (2/183).

items.description: 'I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth as a Muslim with sincere faith, and I am not...
items.content_markdown:
### 2. Second Supplication

> **وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ حَنِيفًا، وَمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، إِنَّ صَلَاتِي، وَنُسُكِي، وَمَحْيَايَ، وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَبِذَلِكَ أُمِرْتُ وَأَنَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، اللهُمَّ أَنْتَ الْمَلِكُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ أَنْتَ رَبِّي، وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي، وَاعْتَرَفْتُ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي ذُنُوبِي جَمِيعًا، إِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، وَاهْدِنِي لِأَحْسَنِ الْأَخْلَاقِ لَا يَهْدِي لِأَحْسَنِهَا إِلَّا أَنْتَ، وَاصْرِفْ عَنِّي سَيِّئَهَا لَا يَصْرِفُ عَنِّي سَيِّئَهَا إِلَّا أَنْتَ، لَبَّيْكَ وَسَعْدَيْكَ وَالْخَيْرُ كُلُّهُ فِي يَدَيْكَ، وَالشَّرُّ لَيْسَ إِلَيْكَ، أَنَا بِكَ وَإِلَيْكَ، تَبَارَكْتَ وَتَعَالَيْتَ، أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ**

"I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth as a Muslim with sincere faith, and I am not among the polytheists. Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. With this I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, You are the Sovereign. There is no deity worthy of worship except You. You are my Lord, and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and I acknowledge my sin. So forgive all my sins, for indeed none forgives sins except You. Guide me to the best of character, for none can guide to the best of it except You. Turn away from me evil character, for none can turn it away except You. Here I am at Your service, and all good is in Your Hands, and evil is not attributed to You. I am by You and to You. Blessed and Exalted are You. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You."
*(Narrated by Muslim 2/185-186)*

The Prophet ﷺ used to recite this supplication in both obligatory and voluntary prayers.

### 3. Third Supplication

> **اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ حَنِيفًا مُسْلِمًا وَمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَبِذَلِكَ أُمِرْتُ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الْمَلِكُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ وَبِحَمْدِكَ**

"I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth as a Muslim with sincere faith, and I am not among the polytheists. Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. With this I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, You are the Sovereign. There is no deity worthy of worship except You. Glory be to You and all praise is Yours."
*(Narrated by An-Nasa'i 1/143. Authenticated by Al-Albani in Sifatu Shalatin Nabi 1/251)*

### 4. Fourth Supplication

> **إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَبِذَلِكَ أُمِرْتُ وَأَنَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ. اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنِي لِأَحْسَنِ الْأَعْمَالِ وَأَحْسَنِ الْأَخْلَاقِ لَا يَهْدِي لِأَحْسَنِهَا إِلَّا أَنْتَ، وَقِنِي سَيِّئَ الْأَعْمَالِ وَسَيِّئَ الْأَخْلَاقِ لَا يَقِي سَيِّئَهَا إِلَّا أَنْتَ**

"Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. With this I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, guide me to the best of deeds and the best of character, for none can guide to the best of them except You. Protect me from evil deeds and evil character, for none can protect from them except You."
*(Narrated by An-Nasa'i 1/141, Ad-Daruquthni 112)*

items.content_markdown:
### 5. Fifth Supplication

> **سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ تَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ وَتَعَالَى جَدُّكَ وَلَا إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ**

"Glory be to You, O Allah. I glorify Your name with Your praise. Blessed is Your name. Exalted is Your majesty. There is no deity worthy of worship except You."
*(Narrated by Abu Dawud 1/124, An-Nasa'i 1/143)*

This supplication **was widely practiced by the companions of the Prophet**, so many scholars prefer to practice this supplication in prayer. Moreover, this supplication is quite short and very suitable for an imam leading many people.

items.content_markdown:
### 9. Ninth Supplication

> **اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الحَمْدُ أَنْتَ قَيِّمُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ، وَلَكَ الحَمْدُ لَكَ مُلْكُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ، وَلَكَ الحَمْدُ أَنْتَ نُورُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ، وَلَكَ الحَمْدُ أَنْتَ مَلِكُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ، وَلَكَ الحَمْدُ أَنْتَ الحَقُّ وَوَعْدُكَ الحَقُّ، وَلِقَاؤُكَ حَقٌّ، وَقَوْلُكَ حَقٌّ، وَالجَنَّةُ حَقٌّ، وَالنَّارُ حَقٌّ، وَالنَّبِيُّونَ حَقٌّ، وَمُحَمَّدٌ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حَقٌّ، وَالسَّاعَةُ حَقٌّ، اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ، وَبِكَ آمَنْتُ، وَعَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْتُ، وَبِكَ خَاصَمْتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ حَاكَمْتُ، فَاغْفِرْ لِي مَا قَدَّمْتُ وَمَا أَخَّرْتُ، وَمَا أَسْرَرْتُ وَمَا أَعْلَنْتُ، أَنْتَ المُقَدِّمُ، وَأَنْتَ المُؤَخِّرُ، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ**

"O Allah, all praise is for You. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. All praise is for You. Yours is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. All praise is for You. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. All praise is for You. You are the King of the heavens and the earth. All praise is for You. You are the Truth. Your promise is true. Meeting You is true. Your word is true. Paradise is true. Hellfire is true. The Prophets are true. Muhammad ﷺ is true. The Hour is true. O Allah, to You I have submitted. In You I have believed. Upon You I have relied. To You I have turned. For Your sake I have disputed. To You I have referred for judgment. So forgive me for what I have done in the past and what I will do in the future, what I have concealed and what I have declared. You are Al-Muqaddim and Al-Mu'akhkhir. There is no deity worthy of worship except You."
*(Narrated by Bukhari 2/3, 2/4, 11/99, 13/366-367, 13/399, Muslim 2/184)*

The Prophet ﷺ often recited this opening supplication during night prayer. However, it is also legislated to recite it in obligatory prayers and other prayers.

### 10. Tenth Supplication

> **اللهُمَّ رَبَّ جَبْرَائِيلَ، وَمِيكَائِيلَ، وَإِسْرَافِيلَ، فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ، أَنْتَ تَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ عِبَادِكَ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ، اهْدِنِي لِمَا اخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ مِنَ الْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِكَ، إِنَّكَ تَهْدِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ**

Guide me to the truth in that which they differ, by Your permission. Indeed, You guide whom You will to the straight path."
*(Narrated by Muslim 2/185)*

The Prophet ﷺ also often recited this opening supplication during night prayer. However, it is also legislated to recite it in obligatory prayers and other prayers.

items.content_markdown:
### Etiquette of Reciting Opening Supplication

**1. Combining Multiple Supplications:**
It is sunnah to combine several opening supplications in individual prayer. Or also for an imam, if permitted by the congregation. If the congregation does not permit, then do not recite a supplication that is too long. In fact, it is better to recite a short one. Imam An-Nawawi seems to allude to the hadith:

> **إذا أم أحدكم الناس فليخفف . فإن فيهم الصغير والكبير والضعيف والمريض . فإذا صلى وحده فليصل كيف شاء**
>
> "When one of you leads the people in prayer, let him shorten it. For among them are the young, the old, the weak, and the sick. But when he prays alone, let him pray as he wishes."
> *(Narrated by Muslim 467)*

**2. For Latecomers (Masbuk):**
If you arrive as a latecomer, still recite the opening supplication. Unless you are about to go into ruku' immediately and fear not having time to recite Al-Fatihah. If that is the case, it is better not to recite the opening supplication, but try to complete reciting Al-Fatihah. Because reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar of prayer.

**3. Joining in Non-Standing Positions:**
If you find the imam not standing, for example in ruku', or sitting between two prostrations, or prostrating, then join the imam's position directly and recite what the imam recites. There is no need to recite the opening supplication at that time.

**4. In Funeral Prayer:**
The Shafi'i scholars differed regarding the recommendation to recite the opening supplication during funeral prayer. According to An-Nawawi, what is more correct is that it is not necessary to recite it, because funeral prayer should be brief.

**5. Not Obligatory:**
Reciting the opening supplication is sunnah, not obligatory. If someone omits it, there is no need for sujud sahwi (prostration of forgetfulness).

**6. Recited Silently:**
What is in accordance with the sunnah is that the opening supplication is recited silently (sirr). If recited loudly (jahr), it is makruh (disliked), but does not invalidate the prayer.

items.description: It is legislated to recite isti'adzah before reciting the Quran, both inside and outside prayer...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Isti'adzah in Prayer

It is legislated to recite isti'adzah before reciting the Quran, both inside and outside prayer, including before reciting Al-Fatihah in prayer. However, scholars differ regarding the ruling on reciting isti'adzah before reciting the Quran.

**First Opinion: Obligatory**

Some scholars hold it is obligatory, using as evidence the verse:

> **فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاَللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ**
>
> "So when you recite the Quran, seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the expelled"
> *(QS. An Nahl: 98)*

This verse uses the command form (فَاسْتَعِذْ), and the basic ruling for commands is obligation. This is the opinion of Atha', Sufyan Ats Tsauri, and some Hanbali scholars.

**Second Opinion: Sunnah (Jumhur Scholars)**

The majority of scholars, including the Hanafiyyah, Shafi'iyyah, and the relied-upon opinion of the Hanbali madhhab, hold that it is sunnah. Among the factors diverting its ruling from obligation is the claim of consensus (ijma) that the salaf did not consider it obligatory, and there are several hadiths indicating that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sometimes did not recite isti'adzah before reciting the Quran. Among them is the hadith of 'Aishah:

> **كان رسولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَستفتِحُ الصلاةَ بالتكبيرِ , والقِراءةَ ب "الحمدُ للهِ ربِّ العالَمينَ "**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to begin prayer with takbir, then recite 'alhamdulillahi rabbil 'alamin...'"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 498)*

Therefore, the more correct view, inshaAllah, is that isti'adzah in prayer is sunnah, not obligatory.

items.title: Wording of Isti'adzah
items.description: There are several types of isti'adzah recitation that are legislated...
items.content_markdown:
### Wording of Isti'adzah

There are several types of isti'adzah recitation that are legislated:

**1. First Wording (Jumhur)**

> **أَعُوذُ بِاَللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ**
>
> */a'uudzubillaahi minas syaithaanir rajiim/*
>
> "I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the expelled"

This is chosen by Imam Ash Shafi'i and Abu Hanifah, using as evidence QS. An Nahl: 98. Shaykh Al Albani noted this wording is authentic from the athar of Umar bin Khattab.

**2. Second Wording (Imam Ahmad)**

> **أعوذُ باللهِ السَّمِيعِ العَلِيمِ مِنَ الشيطانِ الرَّجِيمِ**
>
> */a'uudzubillaahis samii'il 'aliimi minas syaithaanir rajiim/*
>
> "I seek refuge with Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan, the expelled"

Chosen by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Umar. Hadith narrated by Abu Daud & Tirmidzi (Sahih).

**3. Third Wording**

> **أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم؛ من هَمْزِه، ونَفْخِه، ونَفْثِه**
>
> */a'uudzubillaahi minas syaithaanir rajiim min hamzihi wa nafkhihi wa naftsihi/*
>
> "I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the expelled, from his madness, his arrogance, and his poetry"
> *(Narrated by Ahmad, Hasan)*

Meaning: *Al Hamzu* (madness/insanity), *An Nafkhu* (arrogance), *An Naftsu* (poetry).

**4. Fourth Wording (Complete)**

> **أعوذُ باللهِ السَّمِيعِ العَلِيمِ مِنَ الشيطانِ الرَّجِيمِ من هَمْزِه، ونَفْخِه، ونَفْثِه**
>
> Combination of "As-Sami' Al-Alim" with additional protection from madness, arrogance, and poetry.

**5. Fifth Wording**

> **أعوذُ باللهِ السَّمِيعِ العَلِيمِ مِنَ الشيطانِ الرَّجِيمِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ**
>
> Adding *Innahu Huwas Samii'ul 'Aliim* at the end. (QS. Fushilat: 36).

**6. Sixth Wording**

> **أَسْتَعِيْذُ بِاَللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ**
>
> */asta'iidzu billahi/* (replacing a'udzu with asta'idzu).

**Conclusion:**

The above wordings may all be used. However, what matches the Prophet's ﷺ practice is more virtuous.

items.title: Silent or Audible Recitation?
items.description: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the companions did not recite isti'adzah audibly...
items.content_markdown:
### Silent or Audible Recitation?

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the companions **did not recite isti'adzah audibly**.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah explained that routinely reciting isti'adzah audibly contradicts the sunnah. However, if done **occasionally** for the purpose of teaching (ta'lim), it is permissible. Just as Umar bin Khattab sometimes recited the opening supplication audibly, and Ibn Umar and Abu Hurairah sometimes recited isti'adzah audibly.

As for doing it routinely (continuously), there is no narration of this from the Prophet ﷺ.

items.title: In Every Rak'ah or Only the First?
items.description: Scholars differ on whether isti'adzah should be recited in every rak'ah or only in the first rak'ah...
items.content_markdown:
### In Every Rak'ah or Only the First?

Scholars differ on whether isti'adzah should be recited in every rak'ah or only in the first rak'ah.

**First Opinion: In Every Rak'ah**

Some scholars, including the Shafi'iyyah and Hanabilah, hold that isti'adzah should be recited in every rak'ah before reciting Al-Fatihah. Their evidence is the general command in the verse "So when you recite the Quran, seek refuge..." which applies to every recitation.

**Second Opinion: Only in the First Rak'ah**

Other scholars, including the Hanafiyyah and Malikiyyah, hold that isti'adzah is only recited in the first rak'ah. Their evidence is that the Prophet ﷺ only recited it at the beginning of prayer.

**The Correct View:**

The stronger opinion is that isti'adzah is recited only in the first rak'ah, as this was the consistent practice of the Prophet ﷺ. However, if someone recites it in every rak'ah, there is no harm, as it falls under the general command of the verse.

title: Basmalah

items.title: Is It Part of Al-Fatihah?
items.description: Scholars unanimously agree that basmalah is a verse of the Quran...
items.content_markdown:
### Is It Part of Al-Fatihah?

Scholars unanimously agree that basmalah is a verse of the Quran, because basmalah is found in one of the Quranic verses:

> **إِنَّهُ مِنْ سُلَيْمَانَ وَإِنَّهُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ**
>
> "Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed, it reads: 'In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful'"
> *(QS. An Naml: 30)*

However, there is very strong disagreement among scholars regarding whether basmalah is part of Surah Al-Fatihah.

**Jumhur Opinion (Hanafiyyah, Hanabilah, Malikiyyah):**

Basmalah is not part of Al-Fatihah. They use as evidence the hadith:

> **قَالَ اللهُ تَعَالَى: قَسَمْتُ الصَّلَاةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي نِصْفَيْنِ، وَلِعَبْدِي مَا سَأَلَ، فَإِذَا قَالَ الْعَبْدُ: {الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ} ، قَالَ اللهُ تَعَالَى: حَمِدَنِي عَبْدِي**
>
> "Allah Tabaraka Wa Ta'ala said, 'I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant into two halves, half for Me and half for My servant according to what he asks. When My servant says, 'Alhamdulillahi rabbil'aalamiin', Allah Ta'ala says, 'My servant has praised Me'"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 395)*

**Shafi'iyyah Opinion:**

Basmalah is part of Al-Fatihah. They use as evidence the hadith:

> **هِيَ: الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العَالَمِينَ السَّبْعُ المَثَانِي**
>
> "It is 'Alhamdulillahi rabbil'aalamiin' which consists of 7 verses"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari 4474, 4647)*

They count "shiraathalladziina an'amta 'alaihim ghairil maghdhuubi 'alaihim wa laadh dhaaliin" as 1 verse, so basmalah is included in the 7 verses.

Another evidence:

> **إِذَا قَرَأْتُمِ : الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فَاقْرَءُوا : بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ إِنَّهَا أُمُّ الْقُرْآنِ , وَأُمُّ الْكِتَابِ , وَالسَّبْعُ الْمَثَانِي , وَبِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ إِحْدَاهَا**
>
> "When you recite Alhamdulillahi rabbil'aalamiin, recite bismillahir rahmanir rahim, because it is ummul qur'an, ummul kitab and the 7 verses, and bismillahir rahmanir rahim is one of them"
> *(Narrated by Al Baihaqi in Sunan Al Kubra 2181, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Al Jami' 729)*

This hadith explicitly states that basmalah is part of Al-Fatihah, and this is the stronger opinion. However, as has been explained, basmalah is established in some qira'ah, so certainly the difference of opinion in this matter is very broad.

items.title: Is It Part of Every Surah?
items.description: Just as the Hanafiyyah, Hanabilah, Malikiyyah and jumhur fuqaha hold that basmalah is not part of Al-Fatihah...
items.content_markdown:
### Is It Part of Every Surah?

Just as the Hanafiyyah, Hanabilah, Malikiyyah and jumhur fuqaha hold that basmalah is not part of Al-Fatihah, they also hold that basmalah is not part of every surah. However, basmalah was indeed revealed by Allah as a separator between one surah and another.

Among the reasons that basmalah is not part of every surah, scholars have consensus (ijma') that Surah Al-Kawthar consists of 3 verses, thus basmalah is not part of Surah Al-Kawthar.

As for the Shafi'iyyah, they hold that basmalah is part of Al-Fatihah and also part of every surah. Among their reasons is that the Prophet's ﷺ companions compiled the Quran and wrote basmalah at the beginning of every surah, whereas what does not originate from the Quran may not be written in the Quran. And scholars unanimously agree that the basmalah between two surahs is the word of Allah, so it must be considered part of the surah.

items.title: Ruling on Reciting Basmalah
items.description: Shafi'iyyah Opinion: It is obligatory to recite basmalah because it is part of Al-Fatihah...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Reciting Basmalah

**Shafi'iyyah Opinion:**

It is obligatory to recite basmalah because it is part of Al-Fatihah. And since reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar of prayer, prayer is invalid if basmalah is not recited due to deficiency in reciting Al-Fatihah. As in the hadith:

> **لاَ صَلاَةَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَقْرَأْ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ**
>
> "There is no prayer for one who does not recite Faatihatul Kitaab"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari 756, Muslim 394)*

Among the salaf who held this opinion are Al-Kisa'i, 'Ashim bin An-Nujud, Abdullah bin Kathir, and others. The Shafi'iyyah also hold it obligatory to recite Al-Fatihah before reciting any surah from the Quran in prayer.

**Hanafiyyah Opinion:**

Reciting basmalah in prayer is sunnah before reciting Al-Fatihah in every rak'ah. It is sunnah to recite basmalah before Al-Fatihah for seeking blessing (tabarruk) with basmalah. As for other than Al-Fatihah, it is not sunnah.

**Hanabilah Opinion:**

It is sunnah both before Al-Fatihah and before qira'ah (other surahs).

**Malikiyyah Opinion (Well-Known):**

Reciting basmalah before Al-Fatihah or qira'ah is makruh. They use as evidence the hadith of Anas bin Malik:

> **صلَّيْتُ مع رسولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وأبي بكرٍ ، وعمرَ ، وعثمانَ ، فلم أَسْمَعْ أحدًا منهم يقرأُ بسمِ اللهِ الرحمنِ الرحيمِ**
>
> "I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, and I did not hear any of them recite bismillahir rahmanir rahim"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 399)*

However, there is a narration from Imam Malik that he held it permissible, and another narration from the Malikiyyah saying it is obligatory.

**Conclusion:**

The difference in this matter centers on whether basmalah is part of Al-Fatihah or not, and whether it is part of every surah or not. Therefore, regarding reciting basmalah or not reciting it, the matter is broad.

items.title: Ruling on Reciting Basmalah Loudly
items.description: Scholars unanimously agree that basmalah is recited silently (sirr) in silent prayers. However, they differ regarding...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Reciting Basmalah Loudly

Scholars unanimously agree that basmalah is recited silently (sirr) in silent prayers. However, it is well-known among scholars that they differ regarding whether basmalah before Al-Fatihah should be recited loudly (jahr) or silently (sirr) in loud prayers.

**First Opinion (Shafi'iyyah): Jahr (Loud)**
Basmalah is recommended to be recited loudly (jahr). They base this on evidence stating that basmalah is part of Al-Fatihah, so it should be recited loudly like Al-Fatihah. Additionally, they cite a hadith from Abu Hurairah:

> **كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَجْهَرُ بِـ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite bismillahir rahmanir rahim loudly"
> *(Narrated by Al-Hakim 805)*

However, this hadith has weakness in its chain. There is also another narration from Abu Hurairah:

> **كُنْتُ وَرَاءَ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ فَقَرَأَ : بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ , ثُمَّ قَرَأَ بِأُمِّ الْقُرْآنِ... وَيَقُولُ إِذَا سَلَّمَ : وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ إِنِّي لأَشْبَهُكُمْ صَلاةً بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ**
>
> "I prayed behind Abu Hurairah, and he recited bismillahir rahmanir rahim, then recited Ummul Qur'an... After giving salam, Abu Hurairah said: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, my prayer is the most similar to the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ'"
> *(Narrated by Al-Hakim 804, with a sahih chain)*

However, some scholars say that using this hadith as evidence is not sharih (explicit), because what Abu Hurairah meant was the overall practice of his prayer in general, not every specific detail.

There are several sahih narrations that some companions recited basmalah loudly, including Abu Hurairah, Ibn Az-Zubayr, and Mu'awiyah radhiallahu'anhum.

**Second Opinion (Imam Al-Bukhari, Imam Muslim, Hanafiyyah, Hanabilah): Sirr (Silent)**
Basmalah is recommended to be recited silently (sirr), not loudly. They state that there is no sahih and sharih evidence that the Prophet ﷺ recited basmalah loudly. Additionally, there is a hadith in Sahihain from Anas bin Malik radhiallahu'anhu:

> **أنَّ النبيَّ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ وأبا بكرٍ وعمرَ رضي اللهُ عنهما ، كانوا يفتتحونَ الصلاةَ : بالْحَمْدِ للهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, and Umar radhiallahu'anhuma used to begin prayer with Alhamdulillahi rabbil 'alamin"
> *(Narrated by Al-Bukhari 743)*

In Muslim's narration:

> **صلَّيْتُ مع رسولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وأبي بكرٍ ، وعمرَ ، وعثمانَ ، فلم أَسْمَعْ أحدًا منهم يقرأُ بسمِ اللهِ الرحمنِ الرحيمِ**
>
> "I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, and I did not hear any of them recite bismillahir rahmanir rahim"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 399)*

This sahih and sharih hadith negates the loud recitation of basmalah. This hadith from Anas is also more sahih and has stronger chains compared to hadiths stating jahr.

**Third Opinion (Malikiyyah): Makruh Jahr (Disliked to Recite Loudly)**
It is makruh (disliked) to recite loudly. Al-Qarafi said: "What is more cautious is to still recite basmalah to avoid scholarly difference, but it should be recited silently, and it is makruh if recited loudly".

**Conclusion (The Rajih Opinion):**
The correct view is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sometimes recited basmalah loudly and sometimes silently, but most often he recited it silently, so that is more virtuous.

Ibn Qayyim Al-Jauziyah said: "The Messenger sometimes recited basmalah loudly, but more often recited it silently. There is no doubt that the Messenger never made it a routine to recite basmalah loudly in night prayer or the five obligatory prayers, whether traveling or not. The rightly-guided caliphs also recited basmalah silently, as did the majority of the Prophet's companions, and also the majority of the people of that land during the best generations of Islam".

Therefore, what is more virtuous is to recite basmalah silently, but it is permissible to occasionally recite it loudly. Shaykh Abdul Aziz bin Baz stated: "Abu Hurairah's statement: 'my prayer is the most similar to the Messenger's prayer' indicates that reciting basmalah loudly is permissible. However, what is more virtuous is not to recite it loudly".

Shaykh Ibn Baz also continued: "This matter should not become a source of dispute; this matter should be considered a minor difference. What is more virtuous is to prefer the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by not reciting basmalah loudly. However, if on some occasions it is recited loudly based on the hadith of Abu Hurairah, or for the purpose of teaching - that is, teaching people that basmalah should be recited - then all of this is not a problem. And some of the Prophet's companions radhiallahu'anhum used to recite basmalah loudly".

title: Reciting Al-Fatihah
description: Complete guide to reciting Al-Fatihah in prayer.

items.title: Ruling on Reciting Al-Fatihah
items.description: The majority of scholars state that reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar of prayer. Prayer is invalid without reciting Al-Fatihah...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Reciting Al-Fatihah

The majority of scholars state that reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar of prayer. Prayer is invalid without reciting Al-Fatihah. Among the evidence is the Prophet's ﷺ statement:

> **لا صلاةَ لمن لم يقرأْ بفاتحةِ الكتابِ**
>
> "There is no prayer for one who does not recite Faatihatul Kitaab (Al-Fatihah)"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 756, Muslim 394)*

Also supported by the Prophet's ﷺ statement:

> **كلُّ صلاةٍ لا يُقرَأُ فيها بأمِّ الكتابِ ، فَهيَ خِداجٌ ، فَهيَ خِداجٌ**
>
> "Every prayer in which Ummul Kitab (Al-Fatihah) is not recited is deficient, is deficient"
> *(Narrated by Ibn Majah 693, authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Ibn Majah)*

Thus, reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar of prayer, and this is the correct view, insha Allah.

**Opinion of Abu Hanifah:**
He held the opinion that reciting Al-Fatihah is not a pillar of prayer, it is not obligatory to recite it. He used as evidence the verse:

> **فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ**
>
> "So recite what is easy from the Qur'an"
> *(QS. Al-Muzzammil: 20)*

**Response:**
The word فَاقْرَءُوا (recite) here is a mutlaq (unrestricted) expression, while there is a qayd (restriction) in the Prophet's hadiths already mentioned, which state that the Qur'anic recitation obligatory in prayer is Al-Fatihah. According to the principle of usul fiqh: *yajibu taqyidul muthlaq bil muqayyad* (it is obligatory to restrict the unrestricted with the restricted).

**Al-Fatihah is Obligatory in Every Rak'ah:**
Based on Abu Hurairah's radhiallahu'anhu explanation:

> **في كلِّ صلاةٍ قراءةٌ ، فما أَسْمَعَنَا النبيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَسْمَعْناكم ، وما أخفى منا أَخْفَيْناه منكم ، ومَن قرَأَ بأمِّ الكتابِ فقد أَجْزَأَتْ عنه ، ومَن زادَ فهو أفضلُ**
>
> "In every rak'ah there is recitation (Al-Fatihah). What the Prophet ﷺ recited aloud to us, we recite aloud to you. What he recited silently, we have shown you to recite silently. Whoever recites Ummul Kitab (Al-Fatihah), it suffices for him. Whoever adds more recitation, it is better"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 396)*

Shaykh Salih Al-Fawzan said: "Reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar in every rak'ah, and it is authentically narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he recited it in every rak'ah".

items.title: Ruling on Reciting Al-Fatihah for the Follower (Ma'mum)
items.description: Scholars unanimously agree on the obligation of reciting Al-Fatihah for the imam and the one praying alone (munfarid). However...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Reciting Al-Fatihah for the Follower (Ma'mum)

Scholars unanimously agree on the obligation of reciting Al-Fatihah for the imam and the one praying alone (munfarid). However, for the follower (ma'mum), scholars differ in opinion.

**Four Scholarly Opinions:**

**First Opinion:**
Al-Fatihah is not obligatory for the imam, follower, or one praying alone. Whether in silent (sirriyyah) or loud (jahriyyah) prayer. What is obligatory is to recite what is easy from the Qur'an.

**Second Opinion:**
Reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar for the imam, follower, and one praying alone. Whether in silent or loud prayer. Also for those who join congregational prayer from the beginning.

**Third Opinion:**
Reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar for the imam and one praying alone, but not obligatory for the follower at all, whether in silent or loud prayer.

**Fourth Opinion (Rajih - Most Correct):**
Reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar for the imam and one praying alone in both silent and loud prayers. However, it is a pillar for the follower in silent prayer only, not in loud prayer.

**Evidence Considered:**

**1. Command to Recite Al-Fatihah:**

> **لا صلاةَ لمن لم يقرأْ بفاتحةِ الكتابِ**
>
> "There is no prayer for one who does not recite Faatihatul Kitaab"

Shaykh Al-Uthaymeen said: "The Prophet's statement 'there is no prayer for one who does not recite Faatihatul Kitaab' - if we apply the three types of negation, we find that there are people who pray without reciting Al-Fatihah. So it cannot mean negation of existence. Therefore, if someone prays without reciting Al-Fatihah, their prayer is invalid. And this hadith is general, not excluded by anything."

**2. Command to Listen Silently:**

> **وَإِذَا قُرِىءَ الْقُرْآنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ**
>
> "And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy"
> *(QS. Al-A'raf: 204)*

Imam Ahmad commented: "Scholars have consensus that the command in this verse refers to during prayer".

Also the hadith:

> **إنما جُعل الإمامُ ليؤتمَّ به ، فلا تَختلفوا عليه ، فإذا كبَّر فكبِّروا ، وإذا قرَأ فأنصِتوا**
>
> "The imam is appointed to be followed, so do not differ from him. When he says takbir, say takbir, and when he recites, be silent"
> *(Narrated by An-Nasa'i 981, authenticated by Al-Albani)*

**3. In Silent Prayer, the Follower Must Recite:**

Jabir radhiallahu'anhu said:

> **كنا نقرأ في الظهر والعصر خلف الإمام في الركعتين الأوليين بفاتحة الكتاب وسورة وفي الأخريين بفاتحة الكتاب**
>
> "We used to recite Qur'anic verses in Dhuhr and Asr prayers behind the imam in the first two rak'ahs along with Al-Fatihah and a surah, and in the last two rak'ahs we would recite Al-Fatihah (only)"
> *(Narrated by Ibn Majah with a sahih chain)*

**Tarjih (Preference) - Shaykh Al-Albani:**

Initially, the Prophet ﷺ permitted followers to recite Al-Fatihah behind the imam in loud prayers. However, later the Prophet forbade them from reciting any Qur'anic verses in loud prayers:

> **لعلَّكم تقرؤُون خلفَ إمامِكم ، قلنا: نعم يا رسولَ اللهِ ، قال : فلا تفعلوا إلَّا بفاتحةِ الكتابِ فإنَّه لا صلاةَ لمن لم يقرأْ بها**
>
> "Perhaps some of you recite Qur'an behind me? Ubadah bin Shamit answered: Yes, I do, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet said: Do not do so, except for Al-Fatihah. For there is no prayer for one who does not recite it"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari in his Juz', Abu Dawud, Ahmad)*

Then:

> **هل قرأَ معي منكم أحد آنفًا ؟ فقالَ رجلٌ : نعم أَنَا يا رسولَ اللَّه . قالَ : إنِّي أقولُ : ما لي أنازعُ ؟**
>
> "Did any of you recite Qur'an with me in the prayer just now? A companion said: Yes, I did, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet said: I was wondering why my recitation was being contested?"

Abu Hurairah said: "From that time on, people stopped reciting Qur'an with the Prophet in prayers where he recited aloud. And they would recite silently in prayers where the imam did not recite aloud."

The Prophet also said:

> **مَن كان له إمامٌ فقراءةُ الإمامِ له قراءةٌ**
>
> "Whoever has an imam, the imam's recitation is recitation for him"
> *(Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ad-Daruquthni, strengthened by Ibn Taymiyyah)*

**Conclusion:**

The fourth opinion is the strongest. Reciting Al-Fatihah is a pillar for the imam and one praying alone in both silent and loud prayers, but it is a pillar for the follower in silent prayer only. In loud prayer, the follower should remain silent and listen to the imam's recitation.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: "The most moderate opinion is: if the follower hears the imam reciting (loudly), he must listen and be silent. If the follower does not hear the imam reciting (because it is recited silently), he must recite Al-Fatihah. This is the opinion of the majority of the salaf and khalaf."

**Important Note:**
This is an ijtihadiyyah (scholarly) matter of difference, and we should respect the opinion that states that followers must still recite Al-Fatihah in all prayers.

items.title: When Should Al-Fatihah Be Recited?

items.content_markdown:
### When Should Al-Fatihah Be Recited?

A follower must follow the imam, not precede or match the imam. The Prophet ﷺ said:

> **إنما جُعِلَ الإمامُ لِيُؤْتَمَّ به، فإذا كَبَّرَ فكَبِّروا ، وإذا ركَعَ فاركعوا ، وإذا سجَدَ فاسجدوا ، وإن صلى قائمًا فصلوا قيامًا**
>
> "The imam is appointed to be followed. When the imam says takbir, say takbir; when he bows, bow; when he prostrates, prostrate; and if he prays standing, pray standing"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 378, Muslim 411)*

Imam An-Nawawi explained: "In this hadith is the obligation for the follower to follow the imam in takbir, standing, sitting, bowing, and prostrating. And this is done by the follower after the imam does it. If the follower matches the imam or precedes him, his prayer becomes deficient, but does not become invalid."

**Alternatives for Followers Who Must Recite Al-Fatihah:**

For those who hold the opinion that followers must recite Al-Fatihah, they should not recite it simultaneously with the imam's recitation or precede the imam. Scholars provide several alternatives:

**1. Recite During the Imam's Pause in Al-Fatihah:**
If there is a pause (saktah) in the imam's recitation of Al-Fatihah, then during that time the follower recites Al-Fatihah. For example, if between *alhamdulillahirabbil 'alamin* and *ar rahmanirrahim* there is a pause, then during that time the follower recites *alhamdulillahirabbil 'alamin*.

**2. Recite During the Pause After Amin:**
If there is a pause in the imam's Qur'anic recitation (after amin), then during that time the follower recites Al-Fatihah. The first and second alternatives are most virtuous, as they still implement the evidence commanding followers to listen to the imam's recitation.

**3. Recite When the Imam Recites Other Verses:**
If the above two alternatives are not possible, then the follower may recite Al-Fatihah when the imam is reciting Qur'anic verses (after amin).

**4. Recite Simultaneously with the Imam:**
If the above three alternatives are also not possible, then the follower may recite Al-Fatihah simultaneously with the imam.

Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih Al-Uthaymeen said: "If you are a follower, it is legislated to recite it immediately after the imam recites Al-Fatihah. So recite Al-Fatihah even if the imam is also reciting. And sometimes this indeed causes difficulty because you are reciting while the imam is also reciting. Especially if the imam uses a loudspeaker. But we say, just proceed and be patient, for whoever is patient will succeed."

**Ruling for Latecomers (Masbuk):**

Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih Al-Uthaymeen explained: "A latecomer, if he enters the prayer when the imam has already bowed, or before bowing but it is no longer possible to recite Al-Fatihah, then in this situation the obligation to recite Al-Fatihah is waived for him".

items.content_markdown:
### Connected or Paused?

It is recommended to recite Al-Fatihah with a pause at each verse, but connecting them is also permissible.

Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih Al-Uthaymeen explained: "Al-Fatihah is recited with proper i'rab (grammar), in order, and connected. And it is recommended to separate each verse, so the reciter will pause 7 times:

1. *Alhamdulillahirabbil 'alamin.* **Pause.**
2. *Ar rahmanirrahim.* **Pause.**
3. *Maliki yaumiddin.* **Pause.**
4. *Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in.* **Pause.**
5. *Ihdinas shiratal mustaqim.* **Pause.**
6. *Shiratalladzina an'amta 'alaihim.* **Pause.**
7. *Ghairil maghdhubi'alaihim waladhaallin.* **Pause.**

Because the Prophet ﷺ recited it by pausing verse by verse, he would pause at each verse. However, if one does not pause, it is also permissible. Because reciting with pauses between verses is only recommended, not obligatory".

items.content_markdown:
### Those Who Cannot Recite Al-Fatihah

Those who cannot recite Al-Fatihah because they are new to Islam or have never been taught must be taught and must learn. Because Al-Fatihah is a pillar of prayer.

**While Unable to Recite Al-Fatihah:**

It can be replaced with other Qur'anic verses that one can recite. As in the hadith of al-musi'u salatuhu (the one whose prayer was deficient because he did not know how to pray), the Prophet ﷺ said:

> **إذا قمتَ إلى الصلاةِ فكَبِّرْ ، ثم اقرأْ ما تيسَّرَ معكَ من القرآنِ**
>
> "When you stand for prayer, say takbir, then recite what you can from the Qur'an..."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 757, Muslim 397)*

**If One Cannot Recite Qur'an at All:**

It suffices to recite tasbih, tahmid, tahlil, and hauqalah to replace Al-Fatihah. This is based on the hadith from companion Ibn Abi Aufa radhiallahu'anhu:

> **جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ: إِنِّي لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ آخُذَ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ فَعَلِّمْنِي شَيْئًا يُجْزِئُنِي مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ. فَقَالَ: " قُلْ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ "**
>
> "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'I cannot recite anything from the Qur'an, so teach me something that will suffice for me'. The Prophet said: 'Say: subhanallah, walhamdulillah, wa laailaha illallah, wallahu akbar, wa laa haula wa laa quwwata illa billah'"
> *(Narrated by Al-Hakim 123, An-Nasa'i 923, graded hasan by Al-Albani)*

Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih Al-Uthaymeen explained: "It is obligatory to teach such a person Surah Al-Fatihah. If time is limited, he may recite any verse other than Al-Fatihah that he can from the Qur'an. If he cannot recite the Qur'an at all, he may glorify Allah by saying subhanallah, walhamdulillah, wa laailaha illallah, wallahu akbar, wa laa haula wa laa quwwata illa billah".

items.title: If the Imam Cannot Recite Al-Fatihah Fluently

items.content_markdown:
### If the Imam Cannot Recite Al-Fatihah Fluently

In some mosques, especially in rural areas, imams are often found who are not fluent in reciting the Qur'an. Of course this becomes a problem because Al-Fatihah is a pillar of prayer.

**Fatwa of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah:**

He was once asked: "Is the prayer of someone whose recitation of Al-Fatihah contains lahn (errors) valid or not?"

He answered: "If the lahn in reciting Al-Fatihah does not change the meaning, the prayer is valid, whether he is an imam or praying alone. Such as pronouncing *rabbil 'alamin wadhallin* or similar.

As for recitations like *alhamdulillahi rabbul 'alamin* or *alhamdulillahi rabbal 'alamin* or *alhamdulullah* and *alhamdilillah* with lam in dhammah or dal in kasrah, or also *'alaihim* or *'alaihum* or similar, these are not considered lahn.

As for lahn that changes the meaning, if the speaker understands its meaning, such as pronouncing *shiratalladzina an'amtu 'alaihim* and he understands that the pronoun here is mutakallim (first person), then his prayer is invalid. If he does not understand its meaning and thinks that the pronoun is mukhathab (second person), then there is scholarly difference regarding the validity of his prayer. Wallahu a'lam".

**Fatwa of Al-Lajnah Ad-Daimah:**

"If you want to pray, choose an imam whose recitation is good. If you know your imam's recitation is not good, meaning he recites with lahn that changes the meaning, such as *iyyaki na'budu* with kaf in kasrah or *an'amtu* with ta' in dhammah or kasrah, then you should not follow him as an imam.

It is obligatory for you to advise him. If he accepts, alhamdulillah. If not, then try by all means to have him replaced with a better imam".

items.title: Ruling on Ta'min (Saying Amin)
items.description: Ta'min here means saying 'amin' after reciting Al-Fatihah. 'Amin' means 'O Allah, grant it'...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Ta'min (Saying Amin)

Ta'min here means saying "amin" after reciting Al-Fatihah. "Amin" means "O Allah, grant it".

**Form of Recitation:**
"Amin" has two forms, qashr (short) and madd (long). Ibn Mandhur explained:

> *aamiin* (read long) and *amiin* (read short) are words uttered at the end of supplication. Al-Farisi said, it is a sentence composed of fi'il and isim, meaning 'O Allah, grant it to me'.

**Ruling in Silent Prayer:**
There is no difference among the fuqaha that in silent prayer, saying "amin" is sunnah, whether for one praying alone, imam, or follower.

**Ruling in Loud Prayer:**
When the imam recites Al-Fatihah loudly, scholars differ regarding the ruling on saying "amin":

**First Opinion (Rajih - Most Correct): Sunnah**
It is sunnah for the imam, follower, and one praying alone. This is the opinion of the Shafi'iyyah, Hanabilah, one opinion of the Hanafiyyah, and also one opinion of Imam Malik.

Evidence:

> **إذا أمَّنَ الإمامُ فأمِّنوا ، فإنه من وافقَ تأمينُه تأمينَ الملائكةِ ، غُفِرَ له ما تقدَّمَ من ذنبِه**
>
> "When the imam says 'amin', then say 'amin'. For whoever's 'amin' coincides with the 'amin' of the angels, his past sins will be forgiven"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 780, 6402, Muslim 410)*

This hadith establishes that the imam says 'amin' and the followers are commanded to say 'amin' when the imam says it.

**Second Opinion: Not Recommended for the Imam**
Not recommended for the imam or one praying alone, what is recommended is for the follower. This is one opinion of Imam Malik and one opinion of the Hanafiyyah.

Evidence:

> **إِذَا قَال الإمامُ: غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ الضَّالِّينَ، فَقُولُوا: آمِينَ، فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ وَافَقَ قَوْلُهُ قَوْل الْمَلاَئِكَةِ غُفِرَ لَهُ**
>
> "When the imam says 'ghairil maghdhubi 'alaihim waladhallin', then say 'amin'. For whoever's saying coincides with the saying of the angels, he will be forgiven"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 782, 4475)*

They argue that in this case, the imam or one praying alone is the one supplicating, so the supplicant does not need to say 'amin'.

**Third Opinion: Obligatory**
It is obligatory for the imam, follower, and one praying alone. This is one opinion of Imam Ahmad.

**Tarjih (Preference):**

The rajih is the opinion of the majority of scholars, which is the first opinion. Because the hadith "when the imam says 'amin', then say 'amin'" is explicit (sharih) evidence stating that both the imam and followers say 'amin'. It cannot be only the followers. From the perspective of this hadith, how can followers say 'amin' if the imam does not say it?

items.title: Ruling on Reciting Ta'min Loudly
items.description: There is no difference among fuqaha that 'amin' is recited silently (sirr) in silent prayer. However, they differ if it is in...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Reciting Ta'min Loudly

There is no difference among fuqaha that 'amin' is recited silently (sirr) in silent prayer. However, they differ if it is in loud prayer:

**First Opinion: Sirr (Silent)**
It is recommended to be silent (sirr). This is the opinion of the Malikiyyah, Hanafiyyah, and a minority of Shafi'iyyah. However, the Malikiyyah only recommend it for followers and those praying alone, while the Hanafiyyah recommend it for followers, those praying alone, and imams.

Their reasoning is that saying "amin" is a supplication, and supplication is originally recited silently (sirr). Based on the verse:

> **ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعًا وَخُفْيَةً**
>
> "Call upon your Lord with humility and in secret"
> *(QS. Al-A'raf: 55)*

**Second Opinion (Rajih - Most Correct): Jahr (Loud)**
It is recommended to be loud (jahr), whether for followers, those praying alone, or imams. This is the opinion of the Shafi'iyyah and Hanabilah.

Evidence:

> **كان رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ إذا قَرأ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ قال آمينَ ورَفع بها صوتَه**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he recited 'waladhallin', would say 'amin' and raise his voice"
> *(Narrated by Abu Dawud 932, Ad-Daruquthni, An-Nasa'i 878, authenticated by Al-Albani)*

**Third Opinion: Both Are Permissible**
Both silent (sirr) and loud (jahr) are permissible. This is the opinion of Ibn Bukair and Ibn al-'Arabi.

**Tarjih (Preference):**

If we return to the evidence, the evidences convincingly show that the imam raises his voice when saying "amin". As in the hadith of Wail bin Hujr radhiallahu'anhu, and the Prophet ﷺ was the imam.

Moreover, the hadith "when the imam says 'amin', then say 'amin'". It is impossible for followers to carry out the Prophet's command if the imam says 'amin' silently and is not heard by the followers.

While the evidence from Surah Al-A'raf verse 55 is general evidence that is specified by these hadiths.

**For Followers:**

Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath-Tharifi said: "Reciting 'amin' loudly for the imam, its hadith is sahih without doubt. As for the follower, there is no explicit hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ".

What exists are narrations from some of the Prophet's companions, including Abdullah bin Zubayr radhiallahu'anhu:

> **أَكَانَ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ يُؤَمِّنُ عَلَى إثْرِ أُمِّ الْقُرْآنِ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ، وَيُؤَمِّنُ مَنْ وَرَاءَهُ، حَتَّى إنْ لِلْمَسْجِدِ لَلُجَّةً**
>
> "Did Ibn Zubayr recite 'amin' loudly after Ummul Qur'an? Atha answered, yes, and the followers would say amin too. Until the mosque would be filled with noise"
> *(Narrated by Ibn Hazm, authenticated by Al-Albani)*

It is also narrated from Abu Hurairah that he used to recite 'amin' loudly when he was a follower and would prolong his recitation.

Thus, wallahu a'lam, the rajih is that followers are also recommended to recite amin loudly. This is strengthened by Shaykh Al-Albani and Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih Al-Uthaymeen.

**Note:**

Some scholars say, if the imam recites 'amin' silently, the follower is still recommended to recite 'amin' loudly. Because reciting 'amin' loudly is sunnah for both imam and follower, this recommendation does not fall just because the imam abandons it.

**For One Praying Alone:**

Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih Al-Uthaymeen explained: "For one praying alone, if he recites Al-Fatihah loudly, he is also recommended to recite 'amin' loudly. And sometimes if one praying alone considers that reciting silently is more virtuous and more conducive to khushu' and further from riya', then in this condition there is an obstacle for him to raise his voice. So if he recites Al-Fatihah silently, he should also recite 'amin' silently, not loudly".

items.title: When to Say 'Amin'?
items.description: For the imam and one praying alone, it is clear - they say 'amin' after saying waladhallin. However, for the follower, scholars...
items.content_markdown:
### When to Say 'Amin'?

For the imam and one praying alone, it is clear - they say 'amin' after saying *waladhallin*. However, for the follower, scholars differ on this matter:

**First Opinion (Rajih - Most Correct): Simultaneously with the Imam**
The follower's "amin" is simultaneous with the imam's "amin". This is the opinion of the Shafi'iyyah and the mu'tamad (relied upon) opinion of the Hanabilah.

Evidence:

> **إذا قال أحدُكم آمين، قالتِ الملائكةُ في السماء آمين، فوافقت إحداهما الأخرى، غُفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه**
>
> "When one of you says 'amin', the angels in heaven say 'amin'. If the two coincide, his past sins will be forgiven"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 780, 6402, Muslim 410)*

This opinion is strengthened by Shaykh Muhammad Nashiruddin Al-Albani. He said: "The people of the past, when they were followers, would say 'amin' loudly and simultaneously with the imam's 'amin'. And not preceding the imam, unlike most people who pray nowadays. Also not being too late from the imam's amin. This is my final opinion on this matter".

**Second Opinion: After the Imam**
The follower's "amin" is after the imam says "amin". This is one opinion of the Hanabilah.

Evidence:

> **إذا أمَّنَ الإمامُ فأمِّنوا ، فإنه من وافقَ تأمينُه تأمينَ الملائكةِ ، غُفِرَ له ما تقدَّمَ من ذنبِه**
>
> "When the imam says 'amin', then say 'amin'. For whoever's 'amin' coincides with the 'amin' of the angels, his past sins will be forgiven"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 780, 6402, Muslim 410)*

Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath-Tharifi explained: "This hadith is evidence that the follower delays saying amin from the imam's 'amin'. Because of the sequence (tartib) indicated by the letter fa". Moreover, originally the follower should not match the imam.

**Tarjih (Preference):**

What is more correct is the first opinion, as explained by Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih Al-Uthaymeen:

"They (who hold the opinion after the imam's 'amin') say, this is like the Prophet's statement *فإذا كَبَّرَ فكَبِّروا* 'when the imam says takbir, say takbir', and it is known that the follower says takbir after the imam finishes saying takbir. So likewise *إذا أمَّنَ الإمامُ فأمِّنوا* 'when the imam says 'amin', then say 'amin'' means the follower's 'amin' is after the imam finishes saying amin.

But this is a weak argument. Because it has been clarified in another hadith text:

> **إِذَا قَال الإمامُ: غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ الضَّالِّينَ، فَقُولُوا: آمِينَ**
>
> "When the imam says 'ghairil maghdhubi 'alaihim waladhallin', then say 'amin'"

So the meaning of *إذا أمَّنَ* is 'when the imam has reached the time to say amin', which is after saying *waladhallin*, or it means 'when the time for saying amin has arrived' then say 'amin'. So saying 'amin' is simultaneous with the imam."

This is an exception to the prohibition of matching the imam. As for if the follower says 'amin' before the imam, scholars unanimously agree that this action is forbidden.

items.title: Supplicating Before Ta'min?
items.description: Shaykh Wahid Abdussalam Bali in his lecture titled 'akhtha'una fis shalah' said: 'Some people who pray, when they reach the...
items.content_markdown:
### Supplicating Before Ta'min?

Shaykh Wahid Abdussalam Bali in his lecture titled "akhtha'una fis shalah" said:

"Some people who pray, when they reach the recitation *ghairil maghdhubi 'alaihim waladhallin*, before saying amin, the imam supplicates silently '*allhumaghfirlii wa liwalidayya ...*' and so on, then the imam and followers say 'amin', as if the followers are saying amin to that supplication. This is a mistake. What is correct is that the imam should not say anything until saying 'amin', then the followers say 'amin'".

**Contradicting Evidence:**

This practice contradicts the hadith:

> **إِذَا قَال الإمامُ: غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ الضَّالِّينَ، فَقُولُوا: آمِينَ**
>
> "When the imam says 'ghairil maghdhubi 'alaihim waladhallin', then say 'amin'"

Also the hadith:

> **كان رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ إذا قَرأ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ قال آمينَ ورَفع بها صوتَه**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he recited 'waladhallin', would say 'amin' and raise his voice"

So it is not legislated to recite supplications between *waladhallin* and saying 'amin'.

**Places to Supplicate in Prayer:**

Moreover, within prayer there are many places that are mustajab (likely to be answered) for supplication that are legislated, such as:
- During ruku'
- During sujud
- Before salam

So there is no need to do it in places that are not legislated. Wallahu a'lam.
