items.title: Ruling on Qur'anic Recitation After Al-Fatihah
items.description: The companions reached ijma (consensus) that it is sunnah to recite Qur'an after Al-Fatihah in the first two rak'ahs of all...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Qur'anic Recitation After Al-Fatihah

The companions reached ijma (consensus) that it is sunnah to recite Qur'an after Al-Fatihah in the first two rak'ahs of all prayers. Ibn Sirin said:

> **لا اعلمهم يختلفون في هذا**
>
> "I do not know of them (the companions) differing on this matter"

**Evidence:**

From companion Abu Qatadah:

> **انَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقْرَأُ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الأُولَيَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ الظُّهْرِ بِفَاتِحَةِ الكِتَابِ، وَسُورَتَيْنِ يُطَوِّلُ فِي الأُولَى، وَيُقَصِّرُ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ وَيُسْمِعُ الآيَةَ أَحْيَانًا، وَكَانَ يَقْرَأُ فِي العَصْرِ بِفَاتِحَةِ الكِتَابِ وَسُورَتَيْنِ، وَكَانَ يُطَوِّلُ فِي الأُولَى، وَكَانَ يُطَوِّلُ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الأُولَى مِنْ صَلاَةِ الصُّبْحِ، وَيُقَصِّرُ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ would recite Al-Fatihah in the first two rak'ahs of Dhuhr prayer and also recite two surahs, making the first longer and the second shorter, and sometimes making one verse audible. He would recite Al-Fatihah in the first two rak'ahs of Asr prayer and also recite two surahs, making the first longer. He would also make the first rak'ah of Fajr prayer longer and the second shorter"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 759, Muslim 451)*

**Ruling on the Third and Fourth Rak'ahs:**

Scholars differ regarding Qur'anic recitation in the third or fourth rak'ah. The majority of scholars hold that it is not sunnah to recite Qur'an in the third or fourth rak'ah, but this practice is not forbidden as practiced by the salaf.

items.title: Surahs That Were the Prophet's Habit
items.description: Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath-Tharifi explained: 'It is legislated for the imam, as well as one praying alone (munfarid), in most of...
items.content_markdown:
### Surahs That Were the Prophet's Habit

Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath-Tharifi explained: "It is legislated for the imam, as well as one praying alone (munfarid), in most of what he does in Fajr prayer to recite from thiwal mufassal, in Maghrib prayer to recite from qisar mufassal, and in other prayers to recite from wasath mufassal".

**Division of Mufassal:**

Scholars differ regarding the terms qisar mufassal, wasath mufassal, and thiwal mufassal. A good opinion is that expressed by Ibn Ma'in, which is preferred by As-Suyuthi in Al-Itqan Fi Ulumil Qur'an:

> **فَطِوَالُهُ إِلَى عَمَّ وَأَوْسَاطُهُ مِنْهَا إِلَى الضُّحَى وَمِنْهَا إِلَى آخِرِ الْقُرْآنِ قِصَارُهُ**
>
> "Thiwal mufassal is (Qaf) until 'Amma (yatasaa'aluun), wasath mufassal is from 'Amma until Ad-Dhuha, and from Ad-Dhuha until the end is qisar mufassal"

However, outside this general rule, there are several surahs that the Prophet ﷺ habitually recited in his prayers, so it is also recommended to follow him in this.

items.title: Surahs for Maghrib Prayer

items.content_markdown:
### Surahs for Maghrib Prayer

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited **Surah At-Tur**, **Al-A'raf**, and **Al-Mursalat** during Maghrib prayer.

**1. Surah At-Tur:**

From Jubair bin Muth'im, he said:

> **سمعتُ رسولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأُ بالطورِ في المغربِ**
>
> "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite Surah At-Tur in Maghrib prayer"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 463)*

**2. Surah Al-A'raf:**

From Marwan bin Hakam, he said:

> **أنَّ زيدَ بنَ ثابتٍ قالَ : ما لي أراكَ تقرأُ في المغربِ بقصارِ السُّورِ ؟ قد رأيتُ رسولَ اللهِ يقرأُ فيها بأطول الطُّوليينِ ! قلتُ : يا أبا عبدِ اللهِ ، ما أطولُ الطُّوليينِ؟ قالَ : الأعراف**
>
> "Zaid bin Thabit asked him, 'Why do you recite short surahs in Maghrib prayer? I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite the longest surah'. Marwan said, 'O Abu Abdullah, what is the longest surah you mean?'. He answered, Al-A'raf"
> *(Narrated by An-Nasa'i 989, authenticated by Al-Albani)*

**3. Surah Al-Mursalat:**

From Ibn Abbas, he said:

> **إن أم الفضل سمعته ، وهو يقرأ : { والمرسلات عرفا } . فقالت : يابني ، والله لقد ذكرتني بقراءتك هذه السورة ، أنها لآخر ما سمعت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ بها في المغرب**
>
> "Umm al-Fadhl heard him reciting 'wal mursalaati 'urfaa'. Then Umm al-Fadhl said, 'My son, by Allah you have reminded me with your recitation of this surah that this was the last surah I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite in Maghrib prayer'"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 763, Muslim 462)*

items.title: Surahs for Fajr Prayer
items.description: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Surah Qaf and At-Takwir in Fajr prayer. 1. Surah Qaf: From Quthbah bin Malik, he said: 'He...
items.content_markdown:
### Surahs for Fajr Prayer

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited **Surah Qaf** and **At-Takwir** in Fajr prayer.

**1. Surah Qaf:**

From Quthbah bin Malik, he said:

> **أنه صلى مع النبيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الصبحَ . فقرأ في أولِ ركعةٍ: والنخلُ باسقاتٍ لها طلعٌ نضيدٌ. وربما قال: ق**
>
> "He prayed Fajr with the Prophet ﷺ. In the first rak'ah he recited the verse *baasiqaatin lahaa thal'un nadhiid* (Surah Qaf verse 10)"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 457)*

**2. Surah At-Takwir:**

'Amr bin Harith said:

> **سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقْرَأُ فِي الْفَجْرِ إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ**
>
> "I heard the Prophet ﷺ in Fajr prayer recite *idzas syamsu kuwwirat* (Surah At-Takwir)"
> *(Narrated by An-Nasa'i in As-Sughra 941, with a hasan chain)*

items.title: Surahs for Isha Prayer
items.description: Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath-Tharifi stated: 'It is makruh (disliked) to prolong the recitation of surahs in Isha prayer as the Prophet...
items.content_markdown:
### Surahs for Isha Prayer

Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath-Tharifi stated: "It is makruh (disliked) to prolong the recitation of surahs in Isha prayer as the Prophet ﷺ forbade Mu'adh". Because what is recommended in Isha prayer is surahs from wasath mufassal.

**The Story of Mu'adh bin Jabal:**

> **أنَّ مُعاذَ بنَ جبلٍ رضي الله عنه كان يُصلِّي معَ النَّبِيِّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم، ثم يأتي قَومَه فيُصلِّي بهمُ الصلاةَ، فقَرأ بهمُ البقرةَ، قال : فتجوَّز رجلٌ فصلَّى صلاةً خفيفةً، فبلَغ ذلك مُعاذًا فقال : إنه منافقٌ، فبلَغ ذلك الرجلَُ، فأَتَى النبيَّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم فقال : يا رسولَ اللهِ، إنا قومٌ نعمَل بأيدينا، ونَسقي بنَواضِحنا، وإن مُعاذًا صلَّى بنا البارِحةَ، فقرَأ البقرةَ، فتجوَّزتُ، فزعَم أني منافقٌ، فقال النبيُّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم : ( يا مُعاذُ، أفتَّانٌ أنت – ثلاثًا – اقرَأْ : { وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا} . و{ سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى } . ونحوَها )**
>
> "Mu'adh bin Jabal radhiallahu'anhu used to pray with the Prophet ﷺ. Then he would return to his people and lead them in prayer. Then he recited Surah Al-Baqarah. A man left the prayer and prayed a lighter prayer by himself. When this reached Mu'adh, he said, 'He is a hypocrite'. When this reached the man, he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we are people who work with our hands during the day and water our fields with our camels. Yesterday Mu'adh led us in prayer and recited Al-Baqarah, so I left, and he claimed I am a hypocrite'. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'O Mu'adh, are you a trial-maker?' Three times. 'Recite *was syamsi wad dhuhaaha* (Ash-Shams) and *sabbihisma rabbikal a'laa* (Al-A'la) or similar'"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 6106, Muslim 465)*

Surah Ash-Shams and Al-A'la are from wasath mufassal.

items.title: Surahs for Dhuhr and Asr Prayers
items.description: From Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri: Conclusion: - Dhuhr Prayer: Rak'ahs 1-2: About Surah As-Sajdah (30 verses), Rak'ahs 3-4: Half of...
items.content_markdown:
### Surahs for Dhuhr and Asr Prayers

From Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri:

> **كنا نحزرُ قيامَ رسولِ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ في الظهرِ والعصرِ . فحزرنا قيامَه في الركعتين الأوليين من الظهر قدرَ قراءةِ الم تنزيل – السجدة . وحزرنا قيامَه في الأخريين قدرَ النصفِ من ذلك وحزرنا قيامه في الركعتين الأوليين من العصرِ على قدرِ قيامِه في الأخريين من الظهرِ وفي الأخريين من العصرِ على النصفِ من ذلك . ولم يذكر أبو بكرٍ في روايته : الم تنزيل . وقال : قدر ثلاثين آيةً**
>
> "We used to estimate the length of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ standing in Dhuhr and Asr prayers. We estimated his standing in the first two rak'ahs of Dhuhr to be about the length of reciting Alif laam miim tanzil (As-Sajdah). And we estimated his standing in the last two rak'ahs to be about half of that. And we estimated his standing in the first two rak'ahs of Asr to be like his standing in the last two rak'ahs of Dhuhr. And in the last two rak'ahs of Asr to be about half of that. In Abu Bakr's narration, Alif laam miim tanzil is not mentioned, but he said: 'about 30 verses'"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 452)*

**Conclusion:**
- **Dhuhr Prayer:** Rak'ahs 1-2: About Surah As-Sajdah (30 verses), Rak'ahs 3-4: Half of that (15 verses)
- **Asr Prayer:** Rak'ahs 1-2: About 15 verses, Rak'ahs 3-4: About 7-8 verses

items.title: Shortening Recitation While Traveling
items.description: Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath-Tharifi said: 'The recommendation of specific surahs for each prayer mentioned above is excepted during...
items.content_markdown:
### Shortening Recitation While Traveling

Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath-Tharifi said: "The recommendation of specific surahs for each prayer mentioned above is excepted during travel. During travel, there is no need to specify particular surahs, rather what is legislated is to lighten the recitation."

**Evidence:**

**1. Mu'awwidzatain in Fajr Prayer:**
There is a sahih (authentic) narration from the Prophet ﷺ that he recited the mu'awwidzatain (*qul a'udzubirabbinnas* and *qul a'udzu birabbil falaq*) in Fajr prayer while traveling.
*(Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud from 'Uqbah bin Amir and authenticated by Abu Hatim)*

**2. Li Iilafi Quraisy:**
There is a sahih (authentic) narration narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah from Ma'rur bin Suwaid from 'Umar that when 'Umar was traveling for Hajj, he prayed Fajr by reciting *li iila fi quraisy*.

**3. Qul Yaa Ayyuhal Kafirun and Qul Huwallahu Ahad:**
There is also a sahih (authentic) narration from 'Amr bin Maimun, that when praying while traveling he recited *qul yaa ayyuhal kafirun* and *qul huwallahu ahad*.

**Conclusion:**
During travel, what is legislated is to lighten the recitation with short surahs, no need to follow the recommendation of long surahs as when residing.

items.title: Recommendation to Adjust to the Congregation's Condition
items.description: It is recommended for the imam to adjust to the condition of the congregation. If there are weak people, sick people, or children...
items.content_markdown:
### Recommendation to Adjust to the Congregation's Condition

It is recommended for the imam to adjust to the condition of the congregation. If there are weak people, sick people, or children, it is recommended to lighten the prayer.

**Hadith:**

> **إذا أمَّ أحدُكم الناسَ فليخفِّفْ . فإن فيهم الصغيرَ والكبيرَ والضعيفَ والمريضَ . فإذا صلَّى وحده فليصلِّ كيف شاء**
>
> "When one of you leads the people in prayer, let him lighten it. For among them are the young, the old, the weak, and the sick. But when he prays alone, let him pray as he wishes"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 90, Muslim 467)*

**Explanation of Imam At-Tirmidhi:**
"This is the opinion of the majority of scholars. They hold that the imam should not prolong the prayer out of concern for causing difficulty to the weak, the elderly, and the sick".

**Explanation of Ibn 'Abdul Barr:**
"Every imam is recommended to lighten his prayer, this is a matter agreed upon by the scholars. And what is meant by lightening is reducing its perfection. As for if there is a deficiency in the prayer, it is not permissible. Because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade prayer like a crow pecking."

Ibn 'Abdul Barr also said: "I do not know of any difference (khilaf) among the scholars regarding the recommendation to lighten the prayer for anyone who becomes an imam for his people, as long as it meets the conditions we explained, which is that the pillars of prayer remain complete."

**Statement of 'Umar bin Khattab:**

> **لا تبغضوا الله إلى عباده ، يطول أحدكم في صلاته حتى يشق على من خلفه**
>
> "Do not make Allah's servants hate Him by prolonging your prayer until it becomes difficult for those behind you (the congregation)".

items.title: Repeating the Same Surah/Verse
items.description: It is permissible to repeat the same surah or verse in prayer, whether in one rak'ah or in different rak'ahs. Evidence: From...
items.content_markdown:
### Repeating the Same Surah/Verse

It is permissible to repeat the same surah or verse in prayer, whether in one rak'ah or in different rak'ahs.

**Evidence:**

From Abu Dharr radhiallahu'anhu:

> **أن النبيَّ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ قام بآيةٍ يرددُها حتى أصبح**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ stood (in prayer) with one verse, repeating it until morning"

The verse was:

> **إِن تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ ۖ وَإِن تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ**
>
> "If You punish them, they are Your servants. And if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise"
> *(Narrated by An-Nasa'i 1010, Ibn Majah 1350, authenticated by Al-Albani)*

Also from Anas bin Malik radhiallahu'anhu:

> **أن رجلا قال يا رسول الله إني لا أستطيع أن آخذ من القرآن شيئا فعلمني ما يجزئني منه قال قل سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله**
>
> "A man said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I cannot memorize anything from the Qur'an, so teach me what will suffice for me'. He said, 'Say: subhanallah, walhamdulillah, wa laailaha illallah, wallahu akbar, wa laa haula wa laa quwwata illa billah'"

This shows flexibility in Qur'anic recitation, including the permissibility of repeating verses.

items.title: Reciting Qur'an in Order
items.description: Scholars differ on whether it is sunnah to recite Qur'an in order (tartib) in prayer. First Opinion: Sunnah to Maintain Order...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting Qur'an in Order

Scholars differ on whether it is sunnah to recite Qur'an in order (tartib) in prayer.

**First Opinion: Sunnah to Maintain Order**
It is sunnah to maintain the order of surahs in recitation. This is the opinion of some Shafi'i scholars.

Their reasoning is that the order of surahs in the Mushaf is tauqifi (divinely ordained), so it should be followed in recitation.

**Second Opinion (Rajih - Most Correct): Not Sunnah**
It is not sunnah to maintain the order of surahs. This is the opinion of the majority of scholars including the Hanafiyyah, Malikiyyah, and the relied-upon opinion of the Shafi'iyyah.

**Evidence:**

From Hudzaifah radhiallahu'anhu:

> **صليت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات ليلة فافتتح البقرة فقلت يركع عند المائة ثم مضى فقلت يصلي بها في ركعة فمضى فقلت يركع بها ثم افتتح النساء فقرأها ثم افتتح آل عمران فقرأها**
>
> "I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ one night. He started with Al-Baqarah. I thought he would bow at one hundred verses, but he continued. I thought he would complete it in one rak'ah, but he continued. I thought he would bow with it, then he started An-Nisa and recited it, then he started Ali 'Imran and recited it"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 772)*

This hadith shows that the Prophet ﷺ did not maintain the order of surahs in the Mushaf, as he recited An-Nisa before Ali 'Imran.

Also from Ibn Mas'ud radhiallahu'anhu:

> **من قرأ البقرة في ليلة فقد أكثر وأطاب**
>
> "Whoever recites Al-Baqarah in one night has done much and done well"

This indicates that reciting surahs out of order is permissible and does not diminish the virtue.

**Conclusion:**
The more correct opinion is that it is not sunnah to maintain the order of surahs in prayer recitation. However, if one does maintain the order, there is no harm in it.

items.title: Brief Pause Before Ruku
items.description: Hanbali and Shafi'i scholars recommend saktah (brief pause) before saying takbir when intending to perform ruku...
items.content_markdown:
### Brief Pause Before Ruku

**Scholarly Opinions:**

Hanbali and Shafi'i scholars recommend saktah (brief pause) before saying takbir when intending to perform ruku.

Shaykh Ibn Al Utsaimin said: "It is sunnah before ruku to pause briefly. But not a long pause, just enough to calm the soul (before ruku)."

Meanwhile, the Malikiyyah and Hanafiyyah hold that this is not legislated.

**Disputed Evidence:**

This matter is based on the hadith from Samurah bin Jundub:

> **أو سكتة إذا فرغ من فاتحة الكتاب وسورة عند الركوع**
>
> "I remember two saktah (brief pauses) in prayer: first when the imam says takbir until he recites (Al-Fatihah), and when he finishes reciting Al-Fatihah and a surah, when intending to perform ruku"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 777)*

**Hadith Status:**

However, this hadith's grade is disputed, because in its chain is Al Hasan bin Yassar narrating from Samurah. Shaykh Abdul Haqq Al Isybili stated: "Al Hasan's hearing from Samurah is confirmed by Ali bin Al Madini, but denied by other scholars."

The more correct view, inshaAllah, is that Al Hasan did not hear from Samurah, as stated by Ad Daruquthni after presenting this hadith: "Al Hasan's hearing from Samurah is disputed. The correct view is that he only heard one hadith from Samurah, namely the hadith about aqiqah."

Therefore, this hadith is weak due to disconnection (inqitha'). This hadith was weakened by Al Albani in Dhaif Abu Daud. Thus, the correct view is that it is not specifically recommended to pause briefly before ruku.

**General Quranic Recitation Guidance:**

However, this falls under the general guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in reciting the Quran, namely that he would pause at the end of each verse. As in the hadith from Umm Salamah:

> **كان رسولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأَ يُقطّعُ قراءتَهُ آيةً آيةً**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite the Quran by breaking it verse by verse"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 4001, Ad Daruquthni 1/651, authenticated by Al Albani)*

Shaykh Al Albani explained: "What indicates the legislation of saktah in this case (before ruku) is the explanation that has passed regarding the Prophet's ﷺ guidance in reciting the Quran, namely that he would pause at each verse. And this saktah, as stated by Ibnul Qayyim, is just enough to restore one's composure (ready for ruku)."

items.title: Ruling on Takbir Other Than Takbiratul Ihram
items.description: Scholars differ regarding the ruling on takbir other than takbiratul ihram or takbir intiqal into three opinions...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Takbir Other Than Takbiratul Ihram

Scholars differ regarding the ruling on takbir other than takbiratul ihram or takbir intiqal into three opinions:

**First Opinion (Strongest): Sunnah**
The ruling is sunnah. This is the opinion of the majority of scholars (jumhur).

**Second Opinion: Obligatory**
The ruling is obligatory. This is one opinion from Imam Ahmad.

**Third Opinion: Obligatory in Fardh, Sunnah in Sunnah**
The ruling is obligatory in obligatory prayers, but sunnah in voluntary prayers. This is another opinion from Imam Ahmad.

**Evidence for Obligation:**

Those who hold it obligatory use as evidence the hadith of Abu Hurairah:

> **كان رسولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قام الى الصلاةِ ، يُكبِّرُ حين يقومُ ، ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يركعُ ، ثم يقولُ: سَمِعَ اللهُ لمن حمدَه. حين يرفعُ صُلبَه من الركعةِ ، ثم يقولُ وهو قائمٌ: ربنا ولك الحمدُ . قال عبدُ اللهِ: ولك الحمدُ. ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يَهْوي، ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يرفعُ رأسَه ، ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يسجدُ ، ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يرفعُ رأسَه ، ثم يفعلُ ذلك في الصلاةِ كلِّها حتى يَقضيها**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ when praying would say takbir when standing, then say takbir when intending to perform ruku, and say: 'sami'allahu liman hamidah' when raising his back from ruku. And when standing he would say 'rabbanaa wa lakal hamd'. Then he would say takbir when prostrating. Then say takbir when raising his head (from prostration). Then say takbir again when prostrating. Then say takbir again when raising his head (from prostration). Then he would do this in all rak'ahs until finishing the prayer"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari 789)*

Also the hadith:

> **صلّوا كما رأيتموني أصلّي**
>
> "Pray as you have seen me pray"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari 631, 6008)*

This hadith uses the command form, so scholars say that the basic ruling for the Prophet's ﷺ prayer procedures is obligatory.

**Jumhur's Response:**

However, the majority of scholars respond that the fiqh principle states:

> **الأمر المجرد يدل على الوجوب إلا لقرينة صارفة**
>
> "A command indicates obligation, except if there is a qarinah (indicator) that diverts from obligation"

And there are 2 qarinah (indicators) that divert from the obligation of this matter:

**1. First Qarinah:**
No narration is transmitted that the takbir practice performed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was done continuously.

**2. Second Qarinah:**
There are many narrations from the companions that they used to leave takbir intiqal.

**Evidence from Companions:**

**a. Hadith of Imran bin Hushain:**

> **عن عمران بن حصين قال صلى مع علي رضي الله عنه بالبصرة فقال ذكرنا هذا الرجل صلاة كنا نصليها مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر أنه كان يكبر كلما رفع وكلما وضع**
>
> "From Imran bin Hushain, he said that he once prayed with Ali bin Abi Talib in Basrah. He said: 'This man reminded us of the prayer we used to practice with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ'. And he mentioned that what was meant was that he always said takbir when rising and when descending"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari 784)*

This hadith shows that some companions used to leave takbir intiqal, so when there was a companion who always said takbir intiqal, they were reminded that this was the practice of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ prayer.

**b. Athar of Abu Hurairah:**

> **عن أبي سلمة,أن أبا هريرةَ كان يُكَبِّرُ في الصلاةِ كُلَّما رَفَعَ ووَضَعَ ، فقلنا : يا أبا هريرةَ ، ما هذا التَكْبِيرُ ؟! قال : إنها لَصلاةُ رسولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم**
>
> "From Abu Salamah, that Abu Hurairah would say takbir in prayer every time he rose and every time he descended. So we asked: O Abu Hurairah, what is this takbir? He answered: this is the way of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ prayer"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 392)*

Abu Salamah is a tabi'i. So this athar also shows that some tabi'in used to not say takbir intiqal.

**c. Athar of Ikrimah and Ibn Abbas:**

> **عن عكرمة, قال :صليتُ خلف شيخٍ في مكةَ ، فكبَّرَ ثنتين وعشرين تكبيرةً ، فقلتُ لابنِ عباسٍ: إنه أحمقُ، فقال: ثَكلتك أُمُّك، سُنَّةُ أبي القاسمِ صلى الله عليه وسلم**
>
> "From Ikrimah, he said: I once prayed behind an elder in Mecca. He said takbir 22 times in his prayer. I said to Ibn Abbas: 'this person is foolish'. Ibn Abbas immediately said: 'tsakilatka ummuk (how unfortunate you are)! This is the sunnah of Abul Qasim ﷺ'"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari 788)*

This athar shows that Ikrimah and Ibn Abbas did not view takbir intiqal as an obligation, although indeed the guidance from the Messenger was so.

**Other Athars:**

In addition, there are other athars showing that Umar bin Al Khattab, Umar bin Abdil Aziz, Al Qasim bin Muhammad, Salim bin Abdillah, and Sa'id bin Jubair did not perfect the takbir (itmaam at takbir), or in other words they left takbir intiqal.

**Conclusion:**

From these explanations, we know that the salaf understood that takbir intiqal is not obligatory, and it was well-known among them that they sometimes left it. Therefore, the strongest opinion in this matter is the jumhur scholars' opinion stating that takbir intiqal is sunnah. Wallahu a'lam.

items.description: Jumhur Opinion: Sunnah. Raf'ul yadain or raising both hands when saying takbir before ruku is sunnah...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling on Raising Hands When Saying Takbir Before Ruku

**Jumhur Opinion: Sunnah**

Raf'ul yadain or raising both hands when saying takbir before ruku is sunnah. This is the opinion of the majority of scholars, from the Shafi'iyyah, Hanabilah, the final opinion of Imam Malik, Al Auza'i, and the scholars of Sham and Hijaz.

**Evidence (Reaching Mutawatir Level):**

Evidence regarding the legislation of raf'ul yadain in this matter is very abundant, reaching the level of mutawatir.

**1. Hadith of Ibn Umar:**

> **أنَّ النبيَّ صلّى الله عليه وسلّم كان يرفعُ يديه حذوَ مَنكبيه؛ إذا افتتح الصَّلاةَ، وإذا كبَّرَ للرُّكوع، وإذا رفع رأسه من الرُّكوع**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ used to raise his hands to shoulder level when beginning prayer, when saying takbir for ruku, and when raising his head from ruku"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 735)*

**2. Hadith of Malik bin Huwairits:**

> **إذا صلَّى كبَّر ورفَع يدَيهِ، وإذا أراد أن يركَع رفَع يدَيهِ، وإذا رفَع رأسَه من الرُّكوعِ رفَع يدَيهِ**
>
> "When the Prophet ﷺ prayed, he would say takbir and raise his hands. When intending to perform ruku, he would raise his hands. And when raising his head from ruku, he would raise his hands"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari, 737)*

**Practice of 17 Companions:**

Imam Al Bukhari has a special book titled "Qurratu 'Ainain bi Raf'il Yadain fis Shalah" or often called "Juz Raf'il Yadain" which mentions narrations about raising both hands when saying takbir in prayer. In it he said:

> **وَكَذَلِكَ يُرْوَى عَنْ سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ نَفْسًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَرْفَعُونَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ**
>
> "Likewise it is narrated from 17 companions of the Prophet ﷺ that they raised their hands (when saying takbir)"

**Not Obligatory:**

However, raising hands is also not obligatory because some companions of the Prophet sometimes left it.

**a. Ibn Umar Sometimes Left It:**

From Mujahid, he said:

> **صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُمَا فَلَمْ يَكُنْ يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ إِلَّا فِي التَّكْبِيرَةِ الْأُولَى مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ**
>
> "I once prayed behind Ibn Umar, he never raised his hands except in the first takbir of prayer (takbiratul ihram)"
> *(Narrated by Ath Thahawi in Syarh Ma'anil Atsar, 1357, with authentic chain)*

**b. Ali bin Abi Talib:**

From Ashim bin Kulaib, from his father, he said:

> **أَنَّ عَلِيًّا رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ كَانَ يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ فِي أَوَّلِ تَكْبِيرَةٍ مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ , ثُمَّ لَا يَرْفَعُ بَعْدُ**
>
> "Ali (bin Abi Talib) once raised his hands in the first takbir of prayer, then after that did not raise his hands again"
> *(Narrated by Ath Thahawi in Syarh Ma'anil Atsar, 1358, with hasan chain)*

**Hadith of Ibn Mas'ud (Authenticity Debate):**

Some scholars hold that raising hands when saying takbir before ruku is not legislated, others hold this is mansukh (abrogated). Based on the narration from Ibn Mas'ud:

> **قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ : أَلَا أُصَلِّي لَكُمْ صَلَاةَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ؟ قَالَ : " فَصَلَّى ، فَلَمْ يَرْفَعْ يَدَيْهِ إِلَّا مَرَّةً "**
>
> "Ibn Mas'ud said: 'Would you like me to teach you prayer as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed?' Then he prayed and did not raise his hands except once"

**Status of Ibn Mas'ud's Hadith:**

Although all its narrators are narrators of Sahih Muslim, scholars differ regarding the authenticity of this hadith. This hadith was:
- Authenticated by Ibn Hazm
- Graded hasan by At Tirmidzi
- Weakened by Ibnul Mubarak, Abu Hatim Ar Razi, Al Bukhari, Abu Daud, Ad Daruquthni, and Ibn Hibban

The issue is the status of the narrator Ashim bin Kulaib, suspicion of tadlis by Sufyan Ats Tsauri, and suspicion of disconnection between Abdurrahman bin Al Aswad and Alqamah.

After deep research, wallahu a'lam, Ibn Mas'ud's hadith is authentic as stated by Al Albani.

**Not Abrogated:**

However, it is still not correct to say that raising hands when saying takbir is not legislated or has been abrogated.

Shaykh Al Albani explained: "It is not unclear about a usul fiqh principle agreed upon by Hanafi scholars and those who oppose the Hanafis (in this matter), as well as followers of the opinion that raf'ul yadain is abrogated, namely the principle: 'it is not permissible to establish abrogation as long as apparently contradictory texts can still be reconciled'. And this is still possible in this case, in two ways:

**First**, we say that the Prophet ﷺ sometimes raised his hands and this was most often practiced, and sometimes he left it.

**Second**, affirmation takes precedence over negation. And this is also a usul principle."

**Conclusion:**

The stronger view is the opinion stating that raising hands when saying takbir before ruku is legislated and its ruling is sunnah, not obligatory, but it is more virtuous to leave it occasionally.

items.content_markdown:
### When to Perform Ruku

Ruku is legislated in prayer, performed after standing and reciting Quranic verses, then saying takbir intiqal, and then performing ruku. Among the evidence is the hadith from Abu Hurairah radhiallahu'anhu, known as hadith al musi'u shalatuhu, about a companion who did not yet understand how to pray, until the Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam taught him the correct and valid way to pray. The Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam said to him:

> **إذا قمت إلى الصلاة فكبر واقرأ ما تيسر معك من القرآن، ثم اركع حتى تطمئن راكعا**
>
> "When you stand for prayer, say takbir and recite what you can from the Quran, then perform ruku with tranquility (tuma'ninah)..."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 757, Muslim 397)*

This hadith shows that ruku is one of the pillars of prayer. If someone abandons ruku or does not perform ruku properly, their prayer is invalid.

**Allah's Command:**

> **يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ارْكَعُوا وَاسْجُدُوا وَاعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ**
>
> "O you who believe, bow down (perform ruku) and prostrate, worship your Lord, and do good deeds, that you may succeed"
> *(QS. Al Hajj: 77)*

Al Alusi in Ruhul Ma'ani said: "The meaning is: pray! Ruku and sujud are mentioned to replace the term 'prayer' because ruku and sujud are the most magnificent and most virtuous pillars" (quoted from Mausu'ah Fiqhiyyah Muyassarah, 2/48).

#### When is Ruku Performed?

By examining the hadith above and another hadith from Abu Hurairah, we know that ruku is performed after standing and reciting Quranic verses, then saying takbir intiqal, and then performing ruku. The hadith of Abu Hurairah radhiallahu'anhu states:

> **كان رسولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قام الى الصلاةِ ، يُكبِّرُ حين يقومُ ، ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يركعُ ، ثم يقولُ: سَمِعَ اللهُ لمن حمدَه. حين يرفعُ صُلبَه من الركعةِ ، ثم يقولُ وهو قائمٌ: ربنا ولك الحمدُ . قال عبدُ اللهِ: ولك الحمدُ. ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يَهْوي، ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يرفعُ رأسَه ، ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يسجدُ ، ثم يُكبِّرُ حين يرفعُ رأسَه ، ثم يفعلُ ذلك في الصلاةِ كلِّها حتى يَقضيها**
>
> "When Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam prayed, he would say takbir when standing, then say takbir when about to perform ruku, and say 'sami'allahu liman hamidah' when raising his back from ruku. When standing upright, he would say 'rabbanaa wa lakal hamd'. Then he would say takbir when descending (to sujud). Then say takbir when raising his head (from sujud). Then say takbir when prostrating. Then say takbir when raising his head (from sujud). He would do this in all rak'ahs until completing the prayer"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari no. 789)*

However, in congregational prayer, the follower (makmum) performs ruku **after** the imam performs ruku. The Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam said:

> **إنما جُعِلَ الإمامُ لِيُؤْتَمَّ به، فإذا كَبَّرَ فكَبِّروا ، وإذا ركَعَ فاركعوا**
>
> "Verily, the imam is appointed to be followed. When he says takbir, then say takbir; when he performs ruku, then perform ruku..."
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari no. 378, Muslim no. 411)*

The letter **ف** (fa) in **فاركعوا** indicates sequence (tartiib). Thus, it is understood from this hadith that after the imam performs ruku, only then does the makmum perform ruku. This means the makmum should not match the imam's ruku movement simultaneously.

items.content_markdown:
### Body Position During Ruku

**1. Bowing the Body**

As mentioned in the hadith of Abu Humaid As Sa'idi radhiallahu'anhu, he said:

> **أنا كنتُ أحفظكم لصلاة رسول الله صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم، رأيته إذا كبر جعل يديه حذاء منكبيه، وإذا ركع أمكن يديه من ركبتيه، ثم هصر ظهره**
>
> "I was the one among you who memorized best the prayer of Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam. I saw him when he said takbir, he placed his hands level with his shoulders, and when he performed ruku, he placed his hands on his knees, then bent his back"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 828)*

**2. Back Straight and Level with the Legs**

The back position should be straight and level with the legs, not tilted and not excessively bent. Based on the hadith from Ali bin Abi Thalib radhiallahu'anhu:

> **كان رسول الله صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إذا ركع؛ لو وضع قدح من ماء على ظهره؛ لم يهراق**
>
> "When Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam performed ruku, if a cup of water were placed on his back, it would not spill"
> *(Narrated by Ahmad, Al Albani in Ashl Shifat Shalat Nabi [2/637] said: "Its chain is weak, but in conclusion this hadith with all its chains becomes sahih thabit")*

**3. Head Level with the Back**

The head should be level with the back, neither raised nor excessively lowered. Based on the hadith of Abu Humaid As Sa'idi radhiallahu'anhu:

> **إذا ركع أمكن كفيه من ركبتيه وفرج بين أصابعه ثم هصر ظهره غير مقنع رأسه ولا صافح بخده**
>
> "When Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam performed ruku, he placed both palms on his knees and spread his fingers while bending his body with his head neither raised nor brought close to his thighs"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud no. 731, Al Albani in Shahih Abi Daud said: "This hadith is sahih except for the phrase 'nor brought close to his thighs'")*

In the hadith of 'Aishah radhiallahu'anha, it is also explained:

> **وكان إذا رَكَع لم يُشْخِصْ رأسَه ولم يُصَوِّبَه ولكن بين ذلك**
>
> "When Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam performed ruku, he neither raised (lifted) his head nor lowered it (excessively bent it), but kept it level between the two"
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 498)*

**4. Hands Placed on the Knees**

The hands should be placed on the knees, not on the thighs or below the knees. As in the hadith of Abu Humaid above:

> **إذا ركع أمكن كفيه من ركبتيه وفرج بين أصابعه**
>
> "When Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam performed ruku, he placed both palms on his knees and spread his fingers"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 731)*

Also mentioned in the hadith of Wa'il bin Hujr radhiallahu'anhu:

> **فاستقبلَ القبلةَ فَكبَّرَ فرفعَ يديهِ حتَّى حاذَتا أذُنيهِ ثمَّ أخذَ شمالَهُ بيمينِهِ فلمَّا أرادَ أن يرْكعَ رفعَهما مثلَ ذلِكَ ثمَّ وضعَ يديهِ على رُكبتيهِ**
>
> "...then the Prophet faced the qiblah, said takbir and raised both hands until they were level with his ears. Then he held his left hand with his right hand. When he intended to perform ruku, he raised both hands as before, then placed both hands on his knees..."
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 726, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Abu Daud)*

**5. Fingers Spread Apart**

The fingers should be spread apart, not pressed together. As in the hadith of Abu Humaid above:

> **إذا ركع أمكن كفيه من ركبتيه وفرج بين أصابعه**
>
> "When Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam performed ruku, he placed both palms on his knees and spread his fingers"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 731)*

**6. Direction of Gaze During Ruku**

Scholars differ regarding the direction of gaze during prayer. Some scholars recommend looking at the place of prostration during prayer. They use as evidence the hadith of Anas bin Malik radhiallahu'anhu:

> **قلتُ: يا رسولَ اللهِ !أينَ أضَعُ بصَري في الصلاةِ ؟ قال: عِندَ مَوضِعِ سُجودِكَ يا أنسُ**
>
> "Anas said: O Rasulullah, where should I direct my gaze during prayer? Rasulullah answered: toward your place of prostration, O Anas"
> *(Narrated by Al Baihaqi 2/283)*

However, this hadith is weak (dhaif) because it contains the narrator Ar Rabi' bin Badr whose status is matrukul hadith. Also with another hadith:

> **دَخَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ الْكَعْبَةَ مَا خَلَفَ بَصَرُهُ مَوْضِعَ سُجُودِهِ حَتَّى خَرَجَ مِنْهَا**
>
> "Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam entered the Ka'bah, his gaze never left the direction of his place of prostration until he exited"
> *(Narrated by Al Hakim 1/479, Ibn Khuzaimah 3012)*

This hadith is also weak because the narration of 'Amr bin Abi Salamah from Zuhair is problematic (ma'lul).

In this matter, there is not a single hadith that is sahih and explicit (sharih) that specifies a particular direction of gaze during prayer. Therefore, in this matter, the ruling is broad. Shaykh Muhammad bin Shalih Al Utsaimin said: "In this matter, the ruling is broad; a person may look in the direction that helps them achieve greater khushu' (concentration), except when sitting, they should indeed look toward their pointing index finger because there is a narration about this" (Syarhul Mumthi', 3/39).

items.content_markdown:
### Tranquility (Thuma'ninah) in Ruku

**Obligation of Tranquility:**

Tranquility (thuma'ninah) is obligatory when performing ruku; in fact, it is a **pillar** of prayer. One must not be too hasty in prayer movements such that there is no tranquility. Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam said:

> **ثم اركع حتى تطمئن راكعا**
>
> "Then perform ruku with tranquility (tuma'ninah)..."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari 757, Muslim 397)*

**The Prophet's Emphasis:**

Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam in many hadiths emphasized to his ummah the importance of tranquility in ruku. Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam said:

> **أتمّوا الركوع والسجود؛ فوالذي نفسي بيده، إِنّي لأراكم من بعد ظهري إِذا ما ركعتم، وإِذا ما سجدتم**
>
> "Perfect your ruku and sujud. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I truly see you from behind my back when you perform ruku and sujud"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 742, Muslim no. 425)*

He Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam also said:

> **أسوأ الناس سرقة الذي يسرق من صلاته". قالوا: يا رسول الله! وكيف يسرق من صلاته؟ قال: لا يُتمّ ركوعها وسجودها**
>
> "The worst thief among people is the one who steals from his prayer." The companions asked: "O Rasulullah, how does one steal from their prayer?" He answered: "By not perfecting their ruku and sujud"
> *(Narrated by Ibn Hibban no. 1888, graded hasan by Al Albani in Ashl Sifat Shalat Nabi, 2/644)*

In fact, in another hadith, an even more severe warning is mentioned:

> **رأى رجلًا لا يتمُّ ركوعَه ، وينقرَ في سجودهِ وهو يصلِّي ، فقال : لو ماتَ هذا على حالهِ هذه ، مات على غيرِ ملَّةِ محمدٍ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلم ، ينقُر صلاتَه كما ينقرُ الغرابُ الدَّمَ ، مثَلُ الذي لا يتمُّ ركوعَه وينقرُ في سجودهِ ، مَثلُ الجائعِ الذي يأكلُ التمرةَ والتمرتينِ ، لا يُغنيانِ عنه شيئًا**
>
> "Rasulullah shallallaahu 'alaihi wasallam saw a man who did not perfect his ruku and pecked at his sujud (because he was so hasty) while praying. Rasulullah shallallaahu 'alaihi wasallam said: 'If this person dies in this state, he dies not upon the religion of Muhammad. He pecks at his prayer like a crow pecks at blood. The example of one who does not perfect his ruku and pecks at his sujud is like a hungry person who eats only one or two dates. They do not suffice him at all'"
> *(Narrated by Ath Thabrani, authenticated by Al Albani in Ashl Sifat Shalat Nabi, 2.642)*

**Minimum Requirement for Tranquility:**

Some jurists (fuqaha) state that the minimum limit for tranquility is the time needed to recite one tasbih completely during ruku (See Mausu'ah Fiqhiyyah Muyassarah, 2/49).

items.title: Duration of Ruku
items.description: Minimum Duration: The minimum duration of ruku is as mentioned for the minimum tranquility requirement. Ideal Duration: ...
items.content_markdown:
### Duration of Ruku

**Minimum Duration:**

The minimum duration of ruku is as mentioned for the minimum tranquility requirement.

**Ideal Duration:**

The ideal duration is that the length of ruku should be approximately equal to the length of i'tidal (standing after ruku), equal to the length of sujud, and equal to the length of sitting between two sujuds. Thus, these movements should have approximately the same duration. As mentioned in the hadith of Hudzaifah bin Al Yaman radhiallahu'anhu:

> **كان ركوع رسول الله صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وإذا رفع رأسه من الركوع، وسجوده، وما بين السجدتين قريباً من السواء**
>
> "The ruku of Rasulullah shallallaahu 'alaihi wasallam, his i'tidal, his sujud, and his sitting between two sujuds were all approximately equal in duration"
> *(Narrated by An Nasai 1068, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Sunan An Nasai)*

**Summary:**

- **Minimum:** Sufficient time to recite one tasbih completely
- **Ideal:** Approximately equal duration with i'tidal, sujud, and sitting between two sujuds
- **Principle:** Not rushing, allowing adequate time for each movement

items.content_markdown:
### Dhikr Recitations During Ruku

Supplications and dhikr recitations that come from authentic hadiths are of several types, which represent **khilaf tanawwu** (variations in practice). Among them:

**First Dhikr:**

Reciting:

> **سُبحانَ ربِّيَ العَظيمِ (ثلاثاً)**
>
> /subhaana robbiy al 'azhim/ 3x
>
> "Glory be to my Lord, the Most Great" (3 times)
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 874, An Nasa'i 1144, authenticated by Al Albani in Ashl Shifat Shalat Nabi, 1/268)*

**Second Dhikr:**

Reciting:

> **سبحان ربي العظيم وبحمده (ثلاثاً)**
>
> /subhaana robbiy al 'azhimi wa bi hamdihi/ 3x
>
> "Glory be to my Lord, the Most Great, and all praise is due to Him" (3 times)
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud 870, Al Bazzar 7/322, authenticated by Al Albani in Shifat Shalat Nabi, 133)*

**Third Dhikr:**

Reciting:

> **سبوحٌ قدوسٌ ربُّ الملائكةِ والروحِ**
>
> /subbuhun qudduus, robbul malaa-ikati war ruuh/
>
> "Most Glorious, Most Holy, Lord of the Angels and Ar Ruuh (Jibril)"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 487)*

**Fourth Dhikr:**

Reciting:

> **سُبحانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنا وبِحَمدِكَ، اللَّهُمَّ اغفِر لي**
>
> /subhaanakallohumma robbanaa wa bihamdika, allohummaghfirli/
>
> "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and all praise is due to You. O Allah, forgive me"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari 817)*

**Fifth Dhikr:**

Reciting:

> **اللهمَّ ! لك ركعتُ . وبك آمنتُ . ولك أسلمتُ . خشع لك سمعي وبصَري . ومُخِّي وعظْمي وعصَبي**
>
> /Allohumma laka roka'tu, wabika aamantu, walaka aslamtu, khosya'a laka sam'i wa bashori, wa mukhkhi wa 'azhomi wa 'ashobi/
>
> "O Allah, to You I bow, in You I believe, to You I submit. My hearing, sight, mind, bones, and nerves are humbled before You"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 771)*

**Sixth Dhikr:**

Reciting:

> **اللَّهمَّ لَك رَكعتُ ، وبِك آمنتُ ، ولَك أسلمتُ وعليكَ توَكلتُ أنتَ ربِّي خشعَ سمعي وبصري ودمي ولحمي وعظمي وعصبي للَّهِ ربِّ العالمينَ**
>
> /Allohumma laka roka'tu, wabika aamantu, walaka aslamtu, wa 'alaika tawakkaltu, wa anta robbi, khosya'a laka sam'i wa bashori wa dammi wa lahmi wa 'azhomi wa 'ashobi, lillahi robbil 'alamin/
>
> "O Allah, to You I bow, in You I believe, to You I submit, upon You I rely, You are my Lord. My hearing, sight, blood, flesh, bones, and nerves are humbled before You, all for Allah, Lord of the worlds"
> *(Narrated by An Nasa'i 1050, authenticated by Al Albani in Shifatu Shalatin Nabi, 133)*

**Seventh Dhikr (Specifically for Night Prayer):**

Reciting:

> **سبحانَ ذي الجَبَروتِ والمَلَكوتِ والكِبْرياءِ والعَظَمةِ**
>
> /subhaana dzil jabaruut wal malakuut wal kibriyaa' wa 'azhomah/
>
> "Glory be to the Possessor of Power, Sovereignty, Majesty, and Greatness"
> *(Narrated by An Nasa'i 1131, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih An Nasa'i 1131)*

**Ruling on Reciting These Dhikr:**

Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath Tharifi said: "Dhikr during ruku is **sunnah mu'akkadah** (confirmed sunnah). This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, Malik, and Ash Shafi'i. So if it is omitted, there is no sin and the prayer remains valid. Whether omitted due to forgetfulness or intentionally... Whereas Imam Ahmad and Ishaq said it is obligatory; if omitted intentionally, the prayer is invalid, but if due to forgetfulness, it is not invalid" (Shifatu Shalatin Nabi lit Tharify, 122-123).

**Which is More Virtuous: Reciting One Dhikr or Combining Them?**

Some scholars recommend unconditionally combining all the available dhikr. Ibn al-Qayyim in Zaadul Ma'ad (1/37) mentioned:

> **وكان يقول: (سبحان ربي العظيم) . وتارة يقول مع ذلك، أو مقتصراً عليه: (سبحانك اللهم ربنا! وبحمدك، اللهم! اغفر لي)**
>
> "The Prophet would recite 'subhaana robbi al 'azhim' and sometimes he would combine it with 'subhaanallahumma robbana wabihamdika, allohummaghfirli' or sometimes he would suffice with only the first one"
> *(quoted from Ashlu Shifatis Shalat, 2/649)*

Imam An Nawawi in Al Adzkar said:

> **والأفضل أن يجمع بين هذه الأذكار كلها؛ إن تمكن، وكذا ينبغي أن يفعل في أذكار جميع الأبواب**
>
> "The most virtuous is to combine all these dhikr if possible. One should also apply this to dhikr in all other chapters"

However, what is more correct and more virtuous is to **sometimes** recite dhikr A, **sometimes** recite dhikr B, **sometimes** recite dhikr C, etc. The scholarly opinions recommending combination were commented upon by 'Allamah Shiddiq Hasan Khan in Nazilul Abrar (84):

> **يأتي مرة بهذه، وبتلك أخرى. ولا أرى دليلاً على الجمع. وقد كان رسول الله صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لا يجمعها في ركن واحد؛ بل يقول هذا مرة، وهذا مرة، والاتباع خير من الابتداع**
>
> "What is more correct is to sometimes recite this dhikr and sometimes recite that one. I see no evidence supporting the opinion of combining them. Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam never combined them in one pillar; rather, he would sometimes recite this and sometimes recite that. Following (the Prophet's example) is better than innovating"
> *(quoted from Ashlu Shifatis Shalat, 2/649)*

This opinion of Shiddiq Hasan Khan is also strengthened by Al Albani rahimahullah.

items.content_markdown:
### Prohibition of Reciting Quran During Ruku

**Clear Prohibition:**

During ruku, it is prohibited to recite Quranic verses, just as it is also prohibited during sujud. From Ali bin Abi Thalib radhiallahu'anhu, he said:

> **نَهَانِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ رَاكِعًا أَوْ سَاجِدًا**
>
> "Rasulullah Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam forbade me from reciting the Quran while in ruku or sujud"
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 480)*

At Tirmidhi said: "This is the opinion of the Companions of the Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam, the Tabi'in, and those after them; they prohibited reciting the Quran during ruku and sujud" (quoted from Ashl Shifat Shalat Nabi, 2/669).

**Applies to All Prayers:**

This prohibition applies to both obligatory prayers and voluntary prayers. Al Albani said: "What is apparent is that there is no difference between obligatory and voluntary prayers in this matter, because the hadith is general. This opinion is disputed by Atha', who said: I do not prohibit you from reciting the Quran during ruku or sujud in voluntary prayers" (Ashl Shifat Shalat Nabiy, 2/669).

**Wisdom Behind the Prohibition:**

**1. To Focus on Dhikr and Supplication**

Among the wisdom of this prohibition is so that during ruku and sujud, a person occupies themselves with dhikr and supplication. Abdullah bin Abbas radhiallahu'anhuma said:

> **ألا وإني نُهيتُ أن أقرأَ القرآنَ راكعًا أو ساجدًا, فأما الركوعُ فعظموا فيه الربَّ عز وجل وأما السجودُ فاجتهدوا في الدعاءِ فقَمِنٌ أن يستجابَ لكم**
>
> "Know that I was forbidden by the Prophet from reciting the Quran during ruku and sujud. As for ruku, glorify the Lord 'Azza wa Jalla abundantly therein. As for sujud, strive hard in supplication, for it is most worthy of being answered"
> *(Narrated by Muslim 479)*

Therefore, besides the dhikr recitations mentioned above, it is also permissible and recommended during ruku to abundantly recite dhikr taught by the Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam, which generally glorifies Allah without being limited to specific wording (Shifat Shalat Nabi lit Tharifiy, 125).

**2. Ruku and Sujud are Positions of Ultimate Humility**

Scholars also mention other wisdom behind this prohibition. Al Mulla Ali Al Qari explained: "Al Khathabi said that the wisdom of this prohibition is because ruku and sujud are both positions of the utmost humility and self-abasement, which should be dedicated specifically to dhikr and tasbih. The Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam prohibited reciting the Quran during these positions as if he disliked mixing Allah's speech with human speech in one place, as if they were equal. Ath Thibi also mentioned that this is also prohibited while standing" (Mirqatul Mafatih Syarah Misykatul Mashabih, 1/711).

items.content_markdown:
### Making Supplication During Ruku

**Permissibility of Supplication:**

Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath Tharifi explained: "The Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam (during ruku) recited:

> **سُبحانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنا وبِحَمدِكَ، اللَّهُمَّ اغفِر لي**
>
> "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and all praise is due to You. O Allah, forgive me"
> *(Narrated by Al Bukhari 817)*

This shows that ruku is an excellent place for supplication. Therefore, a person may make supplication during ruku with any supplications they can, while also abundantly reciting dhikr glorifying Allah Jalla wa 'Ala. This does not negate the hadith 'As for ruku, glorify the Lord therein.' Because this supplication is an **addition** to the dhikr glorifying Allah, as mentioned by the Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam. Thus, both are combined. The phrase 'O Allah, forgive me' (in the ruku dhikr) applies the verse of Allah Ta'ala (meaning): 'So glorify the praises of your Lord and ask His forgiveness' (QS. An Nashr: 3)" (Shifat Shalat Nabi lit Tharify, 126).

**Not Contradictory:**

This does not contradict the hadith "As for ruku, glorify the Lord therein." The supplication is an **addition** to glorifying Allah, as stated by the Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam. Both are combined.

**Application of Quranic Verse:**

The phrase "O Allah, forgive me" (in the ruku dhikr) applies Allah Ta'ala's command:

> **فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ**
>
> "So glorify the praises of your Lord and ask His forgiveness"
> *(QS. An Nashr: 3)*

**Conclusion:**

Therefore, it is also permissible during ruku to make abundant supplication, with:
- Supplications taught by the Prophet Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam
- Other general supplications using Arabic language
- While continuing to abundantly glorify Allah

May this brief explanation be beneficial. Wabillahi at taufiq was sadaad.

***

**Primary References:**
- Mausu'ah Fiqhiyyah Muyassarah, Shaykh Husain Al 'Awaisyah
- Ashlu Shifati Shalatin Nabi Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam, Shaykh Muhammad Nashiruddin Al Albani
- Shifatu Shalatin Nabi Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam, Shaykh Muhammad Nashiruddin Al Albani
- Shifatu Shalatin Nabi Shallallahu'alaihi Wasallam, Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath Tharify

items.title: Obligation of Tuma’ninah in I’tidal
items.description: I'tidal is the movement of raising the body after ruku' until standing up again with the back straight...
items.content_markdown:
### Obligation of Tuma’ninah in I’tidal, Until the Back is Straight

I’tidal is the movement of raising the body after ruku' until standing up again with the back straight. In the hadith of Abu Humaid As Sa’idi radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **فإِذا رفَع رأسه استوى قائماً حتى يعود كلّ فقار مكانه**
>
> "When the Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam raised his head (from ruku') to stand until every vertebra returned to its place."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 828)*

Allah ‘Azza wa Jallla and His Messenger shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam criticized those who do not perform i’tidal until their backs are straight while they are able to. Whether because their prayer is too fast, hasty, or due to lack of attention in their prayer matters. In a hadith from Abu Hurairah radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam said:

> **إن الله لا ينظرُ يوم القيامة إلى مَن لا يقيم صُلبَه بين ركوعه وسجودِه**
>
> "Verily, on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will not look at the one who does not straighten his spine between his bowing and prostration."
> *(HR. Tirmidzi no. 2678, Abu Ya’la in his Musnad no. 3624, Ath Thabrani in Al Ausath no. 5991. Authenticated by Al Albani in Silsilah Ahadits Shahihah no. 2536)*

From ‘Ali bin Syaiban radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **خرَجنا حتى قدِمنا على رسولِ اللَّهِ صلَّى اللَّهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ ، فبايَعناهُ وصلَّينا خلفَهُ ، فلَمحَ بمؤخَّرِ عينِهِ رجلًا ، لا يقيمُ صلاتَهُ ، – يعني صلبَهُ – في الرُّكوعِ والسُّجودِ ، فلمَّا قضى النَّبيُّ صلَّى اللَّهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ الصَّلاةَ ، قالَ : يا معشرَ المسلِمينَ لا صلاةَ لمن لا يقيمُ صلبَهُ في الرُّكوعِ والسُّجودِ**
>
> "We traveled until we came to the Messenger of Allah shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam. Then we pledged allegiance to him and prayed behind him. When praying, he glanced at a man who did not straighten his prayer - meaning his spine - in ruku' and sujud. When the Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam finished the prayer, he said: 'O assembly of Muslims, there is no prayer for the one who does not straighten his spine in ruku' and sujud'."
> *(HR. Ibn Majah no. 718, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Ibni Majah)*

In another narration, from Abu Mas’ud Al Badri radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam said:

> **لا تُجْزِىءُ صلاةٌ لا يُقيم ُالرجلُ فيها يعني : صُلْبَهُ في الركوعِ والسجودِ**
>
> "The prayer of a man is not valid in which he does not straighten - meaning: his spine - in ruku' and sujud."
> *(HR. Tirmidzi no. 265, Abu Daud no. 855, At Tirmidzi said: "hasan sahih")*

Ibnul Qayyim rahimahullah after citing this narration of Abu Mas’ud said:

> **هذا نص صريح في أن الرفع من الركوع وبين السجود الاعتدال فيه والطمأنينة فيه ركن لا تصح الصلاة إلا به**
>
> "This hadith is clear evidence that straightening the back and tuma’ninah in i’tidal is a pillar (rukun) in prayer, prayer is not valid without it."
> *(Ash Shalatu wa Ahkamu Tarikiha, 1/122)*

items.description: Evidences regarding the legislation of raf’ul yadain (raising hands) in this matter are very many...
items.content_markdown:
### Raising Hands When Rising From Ruku'

Evidences regarding the legislation of raf’ul yadain (raising hands) in this matter are very many. Among the evidences is the hadith from Ibn Umar radhiallahu’anhuma,

> **أنَّ النبيَّ صلّى الله عليه وسلّم كان يرفعُ يديه حذوَ مَنكبيه؛ إذا افتتح الصَّلاةَ، وإذا كبَّرَ للرُّكوع، وإذا رفع رأسه من الرُّكوع**
>
> "The Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam usually when starting prayer, when saying takbir for ruku', and when raising his head from ruku', he would raise both his hands parallel to his shoulders"
> *(HR. Bukhari no.735)*

Also the hadith from Malik bin Huwairits radhiallahu’anhu,

> **إذا صلَّى كبَّر ورفَع يدَيهِ، وإذا أراد أن يركَع رفَع يدَيهِ، وإذا رفَع رأسَه من الرُّكوعِ رفَع يدَيهِ**
>
> "The Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam when praying he said takbir and raised his hands. When he wanted to bow (ruku'), he raised his hands. And when he raised his head from ruku' he raised his hands"
> *(HR. Al Bukhari, 737)*

However, raising hands here is not obligatory because some of the Prophet's companions sometimes omitted it. Among them is Ibn Umar radhiyallahu’anhu, who narrated the hadith about raf’ul yadain, he sometimes omitted it. From Mujahid, he said:

> **صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُمَا فَلَمْ يَكُنْ يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ إِلَّا فِي التَّكْبِيرَةِ الْأُولَى مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ**
>
> "I prayed behind Ibn Umar radhiallahu ‘anhuma, he did not raise his hands except in the first takbir of the prayer (takbiratul ihram)"
> *(HR. Ath Thahawi in Syarh Ma’anil Atsar, 1357, with a sahih sanad)*

items.title: Reciting Tasmi’ When Rising From Ruku'
items.description: Discussion on the ruling of reciting tasmi' and tahmid for imam, makmum, and munfarid...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting Tasmi’ When Rising From Ruku'

In ruku there is the tasmi’ recitation, which is saying: *sami’allahu liman hamidah* (meaning: "Allah hears those who praise Him"). And there is the tahmid recitation, which is saying: *rabbana walakal hamdu* (meaning: "O Allah, all praise is only for You").

From Anas bin Malik radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam said:

> **إِنّما جُعل الإِمام ليؤتمّ به، فإِذا كبّر فكبِّروا، وإِذا سجد فاسجدوا، وإِذا رفع فارفعوا، وإِذا قال: سمع الله لمن حمده، فقولوا: ربّنا ولك الحمد، وإِذا صلّى قاعداً فصلّوا قعوداً أجمعُون**
>
> "Verily the imam is appointed to be followed. If he says takbir then say takbir. If he prostrates then prostrate. If he rises (from ruku or sujud) then rise. If he says: sami’allahu liman hamidah. Then say: rabbana walakal hamdu. If he prays sitting then pray sitting all of you"
> *(HR. Bukhari no. 361, Muslim no. 411)*

In this hadith, two recitations are mentioned: tasmi’ (*sami’allahu liman hamidah*) and tahmid (*rabbana walakal hamdu*). Here scholars differ in opinion regarding the ruling of tasmi’ and tahmid into 2 opinions:

**First Opinion:** Hanbali scholars are of the opinion that tasmi’ and tahmid are obligatory for the imam and munfarid (person praying alone). However, for the makmum (follower), only tahmid is obligatory.

**Second Opinion:** The majority of scholars (Jumhur) are of the opinion that tasmi’ and tahmid are sunnah. However, they differ in opinion regarding the details.

Wallahu a’lam, the stronger opinion (rajih) is the first opinion, that is tasmi’ and tahmid are obligatory for the imam and munfarid, and the makmum is only obligated to recite tahmid. This is the opinion supported by Shaykh Muhammad bin Shalih Al Utsaimin, Shaykh Muhammad Nashiruddin Al Albani and Shaykh Abdul Aziz bin Baz.

Based on the hadith from Rifa’ah bin Rafi radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam said:

> **إنَّها لا تتمُّ صلاةُ أحدِكم حتَّى يُسبِغَ الوضوءَ كما أمَره اللهُ**
>
> "The prayer of one of you is not complete until he perfects the wudu as commanded by Allah..."

Then in this long hadith it is mentioned:

> **ثم يُكبِّرُ ويركَعُ حتَّى تطمئِنَّ مفاصِلُه وتسترخيَ ثم يقولُ: سمِعَ اللهُ لِمَن حمِدَه**
>
> "Then he says takbir and bows until his joints are at ease and relaxed, then he says: sami’allahu liman hamidah"
> *(HR. Abu Daud no. 857, authenticated by Al Albani in Shahih Abi Daud)*

So this hadith indicates the obligation of the tasmi‘ recitation, prayer is not complete without it.

Also based on the hadith of Abu Hurairah radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **ان رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم إذا قامَ إلى الصَّلاةِ يُكبِّرُ حينَ يقومُ، ثم يُكبِّرُ حينَ يركَعُ، ثم يقولُ: سمِعَ اللهُ لِمَن حَمِدَه، حين يرفَعُ صُلْبَه مِن الرُّكوعِ، ثم يقولُ وهو قائمٌ: ربَّنا ولك الحمدُ**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam when standing for prayer he said takbir when standing, and said takbir when bowing, then he said: sami’allahu liman hamidah, when raising his spine from ruku', then he said while standing: rabbana walakal hamdu"
> *(HR. Bukhari no. 789, Muslim 392)*

So this hadith clearly indicates that the imam and munfarid recite tasmi and tahmid. Because the Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam said:

> **صلُّوا كما رأيتموني أُصلِّي**
>
> "Pray as you have seen me pray"
> *(HR. Bukhari no. 631)*

items.title: Tahmid Recitations
items.description: As for the makmum, what is obligatory is only to recite tahmid...
items.content_markdown:
### Tahmid Recitations

As for the makmum, what is obligatory is only to recite tahmid, based on the apparent meaning of the hadith of Anas bin Malik above:

> **وإِذا قال: سمع الله لمن حمده، فقولوا: ربّنا ولك الحمد**
>
> "If he (the imam) says: sami’allahu liman hamidah. Then say: rabbana walakal hamdu"
> *(HR. Bukhari no. 361, Muslim no. 411)*

**First:** *rabbana walakal hamdu*
As in the hadith of Anas bin Malik and Abu Hurairah above.

**Second:** *rabbana lakal hamdu*
From Abu Hurairah radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **إنَّ رسولَ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم قال: إذا قال الإمامُ: سمِعَ اللهُ لِمَن حمِدَه، فقولوا: ربَّنا لك الحمدُ؛ فإنَّه مَن وافَقَ قولُه قولَ الملائكةِ، غُفِرَ له ما تقدَّمَ مِن ذَنبِه**
>
> "Rasulullah Shallallahu’alaihi Wasallam said: if the imam says: sami’allahu liman hamidah, then say: rabbana lakal hamdu. Whoever's statement coincides with the statement of the Angels, his past sins will be forgiven"
> *(HR. Bukhari no. 796, Muslim no. 409)*

**Third:** *Allahumma rabbana lakal hamdu*
From Abu Hurairah radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **إنَّ رسولَ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم قال: إذا قال الإمامُ: سمِعَ اللهُ لِمَن حمِدَه، فقولوا: اللهمَّ ربَّنا لك الحمدُ؛ فإنَّه مَن وافَقَ قولُه قولَ الملائكةِ، غُفِرَ له ما تقدَّمَ مِن ذَنبِه**
>
> "Rasulullah Shallallahu’alaihi Wasallam said: if the imam says: sami’allahu liman hamidah, then say: Allahumma rabbana lakal hamdu. Whoever's statement coincides with the statement of the Angels, his past sins will be forgiven"
> *(HR. Bukhari no. 796, Muslim no. 409)*

**Fourth:** *Allahumma rabbana walakal hamdu*
From Abu Hurairah radhiyallahu’anhu, he said:

> **ان النبيُّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم إذا قال: سمِعَ اللهُ لِمَن حمِدَه، قال: اللهمَّ ربَّنا ولك الحمدُ، وكان النبيُّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم إذا ركَع، وإذا رفَع رأسَه يُكبِّرُ، وإذا قام مِن السَّجدتينِ قال: اللهُ أكبَرُ**
>
> "The Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam if he said: sami’allahu liman hamidah, he said: Allahumma rabbana walakal hamdu. And if he bowed and raised his head he said takbir. And when he stood up from the two prostrations he said: Allahu Akbar"
> *(HR. Bukhari no. 795, Muslim no. 392)*

items.title: Additional supplications in tahmid
items.description: It is also recommended when i’tidal, to recite additional supplications after reciting tahmid...
items.content_markdown:
### Additional supplications in tahmid

It is also recommended when i’tidal, to recite additional supplications after reciting tahmid. There are several additional supplications after tahmid that are authentic from the Prophet Shallallahu’alaihi Wasallam:

**First**, from Rifa’ah bin Rafi radhiallahu’anhu:

> **كنَّا يومًا نُصلِّي وراءَ النبيِّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم، فلمَّا رفَع رأسَه من الرَّكعةِ، قال: سمِعَ اللهُ لِمَن حمِدَه، قال رجلٌ وراءَه: ربَّنا ولك الحمدُ حمدًا كثيرًا طيِّبًا مبارَكًا فيه، فلمَّا انصرَف، قال: مَنِ المتكلِّمُ؟ قال: أنا، قال: رأيتُ بِضعَةً وثلاثينَ مَلَكًا يبتَدِرونها، أيُّهم يكتبُها أولُ**
>
> "We used to pray behind the Prophet shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam. When he raised his head from ruku', he said: sami’allahu liman hamidah. Then a man behind him said: robbanaa walakal hamdu, hamdan katsiiron mubaarokan fiihi (praise be to You O Lord. Praise that is abundant, good and full of blessings). When he finished, the Prophet asked: 'Who was the speaker?' The man replied: 'Me'. The Prophet said: 'I saw thirty-odd angels racing to see which of them would write it first'."
> *(HR. Bukhari no. 799)*

**Second**, from Abdullah bin Abi Aufa radhiyallahu’anhu, he said:

> **كان رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم، إذا رفَعَ ظهرَه مِن الرُّكوعِ، قال: سمِعَ اللهُ لِمَن حمِدَه، اللهمَّ ربَّنا لك الحمدُ، مِلْءَ السَّمواتِ، ومِلْءَ الأرضِ، ومِلْءَ ما شِئتَ مِن شيءٍ بعدُ**
>
> "Usually the Messenger of Allah shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam when he raised his back from ruku' he said: sami’allohu liman hamidah allohumma robbanaa lakal hamdu mil-as samaawaati wa mil-al ardhi wa mil-a maa syi’ta min syai-in ba’du (Allah hears those who praise Him. O Allah all praise is for You, praise filling the heavens, filling the earth, filling whatever You wish more than that)"
> *(HR. Muslim no. 476)*

**Third**, from Abu Sa’id Al Khudri radhiyallahu’anhu, he said:

> **ان رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم إذا رفَع رأسَه مِن الرُّكوعِ قال: ربَّنا لك الحمدُ، مِلْءَ السَّمواتِ والأرضِ، ومِلْءَ ما شِئتَ مِن شيءٍ بعدُ، أهلَ الثَّناءِ والمجدِ، أحقُّ ما قال العبدُ، وكلُّنا لك عبدٌ، اللهمَّ لا مانعَ لِما أعطَيتَ، ولا مُعطيَ لِما منَعتَ، ولا ينفَعُ ذا الجَدِّ منك الجَدُّ**
>
> "Usually the Messenger of Allah shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam when he raised his head from ruku' he said: sami’allohu liman hamidah allohumma robbanaa lakal hamdu mil-as samaawaati wa mil-al ardhi wa mil-a maa syi’ta min syai-in ba’du, ahlats tsaa-i wal majdi, ahaqqu maa qoolal ‘abdu, wa kulluna laka ‘abdun, Alloohumma laa maani’a limaa a’thoyta, wa laa mu’thiya limaa mana’ta, wa laa yanfa’u dzal jaddi minkal jaddu (Allah hears those who praise Him. O Allah all praise is for You, praise filling the heavens, filling the earth, filling whatever You wish more than that, O Possessor of all praise and glory. That is the most deserving thing a servant says. And all of us are Your servants. O Allah there is no one who can prevent what You give. And there is no one who can give what You prevent. And no wealth/power is of use against You, all power belongs only to You)"
> *(HR. Muslim no. 477)*

items.title: Virtue of tasmi’ and tahmid in prayer
items.description: There is a special virtue for those who recite tahmid when i’tidal...
items.content_markdown:
### Virtue of tasmi’ and tahmid in prayer

There is a special virtue for those who recite tahmid when i’tidal. As in the hadith of Abu Hurairah radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **إنَّ رسولَ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم قال: إذا قال الإمامُ: سمِعَ اللهُ لِمَن حمِدَه، فقولوا: ربَّنا لك الحمدُ؛ فإنَّه مَن وافَقَ قولُه قولَ الملائكةِ، غُفِرَ له ما تقدَّمَ مِن ذَنبِه**
>
> "Rasulullah shallallahu’ alaihi wasallam said: 'If the imam says: sami’allahu liman hamidah, then say: rabbana lakal hamdu. Whoever's statement coincides with the statement of the Angels, his past sins will be forgiven'."
> *(HR. Bukhari no. 796, Muslim no. 409)*

Al Khathabi rahimahullah explained:

> **هذا دلالة على أن الملائكة يقولون مع المصلي هذا القول ويستغفرون ويحضرون بالدعاء والذكر**
>
> "This hadith is evidence that the Angels say this statement along with the person praying and ask for forgiveness and are present there for prayer and dhikr."
> *(Ma’alimus Sunan, 1/209)*

And the meaning of "coincides with the statement of the Angels" is that tahmid is recited after the imam says tasmi’. Ali Al Qari explained:

> **(من وافق قوله) وهو قوله: ربنا لك الحمد، بعد قول الإمام: سمع الله لمن حمده،. (قول الملائكة) أي في الزمان. (غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه) أي من الصغائر**
>
> "Whoever's statement (rabbana lakal hamdu) is recited after the imam says sami’allahu liman hamidah coincides with the statement of the Angels in terms of the time of its recitation, then his past sins will be forgiven, that is minor sins"
> *(Mirqatul Mafatih, 3/190)*

items.title: How to Go Down for Sujud
items.description: Scholarly difference regarding whether to place knees or hands first...
items.content_markdown:
### How to Go Down for Sujud

Scholars differ regarding the method of going down for Sujud into two opinions:

**1. Knees First (Majority)**

This is the opinion of Shafi'is, Hanbalis, and Hanafis.

From Alqamah and Al Aswad rahimahumallah:

> **ِحَفِظْنَا عَنْ عُمَرَ فِي صَلَاتِهِ أَنَّهُ خرَّ بَعْدَ رُكُوعِهِ عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ كَمَا يَخِرُّ البَعِيْرُ، ووَضَعَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ قَبْلَ يَدَيْه**
>
> "I remember the prayer of Umar (bin Khattab), that he went down after ruku' on his knees as the camel goes down. He placed his knees before his hands."
> *(Narrated by At Thahawi, authenticated by Al Albani)*

This view is supported by Ibn Al-Qayyim, Shaykh Uthaymeen, and Shaykh Bin Baz.

**2. Hands First (Malikis)**

This is the opinion of Malikis and one view of Imam Ahmad.

From Nafi` rahimahullah, he said:

> **كَانَ إِبْنُ عُمَرَ يُضَعُ يَدَيْهِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ**
>
> "Ibn Umar used to place his hands before his knees."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari in mu'allaq form, authenticated by Al Albani)*

This opinion seems stronger because of the Hadith:

> **إِذَا سَجَدَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلاَ يَبْرُكْ كَمَا يَبْرُكُ الْبَعِيرُ وَلْيَضَعْ يَدَيْهِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ**
>
> "When one of you prostrates, let him not go down as the camel goes down; let him place his hands before his knees."
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud no. 840, authenticated by Al Albani)*

This is the view supported by Shaykh Al Albani. However, this is a matter of ijtihad where difference is acceptable.

items.title: Seven Limbs of Sujud
items.description: The seven body parts that must touch the ground during Sujud...
items.content_markdown:
### Seven Limbs of Sujud

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

> **أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَسْجُدَ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ أَعْظُمٍ؛ عَلَى الجبهةِ – وأشارَ بيدِه إلى أنفِه – واليدينِ، والرُّكبتينِ، وأطرافِ القدَمينِ**
>
> "I have been commanded to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead (and he pointed to his nose), the two hands, the two knees, and the toes of the two feet."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 812, Muslim no. 490)*

The seven limbs are:
1.  **Forehead and nose**
2.  **Right hand**
3.  **Left hand**
4.  **Right knee**
5.  **Left knee**
6.  **Right foot**
7.  **Left foot**

**Note Regarding the Nose:**
Scholars differ regarding the nose. Some consider that the interpretation "nose includes forehead" comes from Thawus (the narrator), not the Prophet ﷺ. Therefore, the majority of scholars consider it *mustahab* (recommended) to touch the ground with the nose, while the forehead is obligatory.

items.title: Method of Sujud
items.description: Details of the correct body position during Sujud...
items.content_markdown:
### Method of Sujud

Based on the evidences, here are the details of the Sujud position:

1.  **Forehead and nose touching the floor.**

2.  **Both hands touching the floor, placed parallel to shoulders.**
    From Abu Humaid As Sa’idi radhiallahu’anhu:

    > **… ثُمَّ سَجَدَ فَأَمْكَنَ أَنْفَهُ وَجَبْهَتَهُ، وَنَحَّى يَدَيْهِ عَنْ جَنْبَيْهِ وَوَضَعَ كَفَّيْهِ حَذْوَ مَنْكِبَيْهِ …**
    >
    > "... then he prostrated and placed his nose and forehead. And he kept his hands away from his sides and placed his palms parallel to his shoulders..."
    > *(Narrated by Abu Daud no. 734, authenticated by Al Albani)*

3.  **Back straight, arms raised and not touching the floor.**
    From Anas bin Malik radhiallahu’anhu:

    > **اعْتَدِلُوا فِي السُّجُودِ، وَلَا يَبْسُطْ أَحَدُكُمْ ذِرَاعَيْهِ انْبِسَاطَ الْكَلْبِ**
    >
    > "Be straight in prostration, and let none of you lay out his arms like a dog."
    > *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 822, Muslim no. 493)*

4.  **Upper arms kept away from the body.**
    From Al Barra bin Azib:
    > **إِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَضَعْ كَفَّيْكَ وَارْفَعْ مِرْفَقَيْكَ**
    >
    > "When you prostrate, place your palms and raise your elbows."
    > *(Narrated by Muslim no. 494)*

    And Abdullah bin Buhainah:
    > **أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ إِذَا صَلَّى فَرَّجَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ، حَتَّى يَبْدُوَ بَيَاضُ إِبْطَيْهِ**
    >
    > "When the Prophet ﷺ prayed, he used to spread his arms so much that the whiteness of his armpits was visible."
    > *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 390, Muslim no. 495)*

5.  **Knees touching the floor.**

6.  **Thighs kept away from the stomach.**
    Asy Syaukani said:
    > **الحديث يدلُّ على مشروعية التفريج بين الفخِذين في السُّجود، ورفْعِ البطن عنهما، ولا خلافَ في ذلك**
    >
    > "The Hadith indicates the legislation of spreading the thighs during Sujud and lifting the stomach away from them. There is no disagreement on this."
    > *(Nailul Authar, 2/297)*

7.  **Toes facing the Qiblah.**
    From Abu Humaid:
    > **... فَإِذَا سَجَدَ وَضَعَ يَدَيْهِ غَيْرَ مُفْتَرِشٍ وَلَا قَابِضِهِمَا، وَاسْتَقْبَلَ بِأَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعِ رِجْلَيْهِ الْقِبْلَةَ**
    >
    > "...When he prostrated, he placed his hands without spreading them out or clenching them. And he faced the toes of his feet towards the Qiblah."
    > *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 828)*

8.  **Heels kept together.**
    From Aishah radhiallahu’anha:
    > **... فَوَجَدْتُهُ سَاجِدًا ، رَاصّاً عَقِبَيْهِ ، مُسْتَقْبِلاً بِأَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعِهِ الْقِبْلَةَ**
    >
    > "...I found him prostrating, with his heels pressed together, facing his toes towards the Qiblah."
    > *(Narrated by Muslim no. 486)*

    *Note:* Some scholars opine that heels should be apart based on a Hadith in Abu Daud (no. 735), but this Hadith is **dhaif** (weak).

items.title: Sujud Recitations
items.description: Authentic variations of Sujud supplications...
items.content_markdown:
### Sujud Recitations

There are several authentic recitations from the Prophet ﷺ in Sujud:

**First Recitation**
From Ibn Abbas radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **فَكَانَ يَقُولُ فِي سُجُودِهِ: سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى، قَالَ: ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ**
>
> *Subhaana rabbiyal a’la*
> "The Prophet ﷺ used to say in his prostration: 'Subhaana rabbiyal a’la', then he would raise his head."
> *(Narrated by Ahmad no. 3514, authenticated by Al Albani)*

**Second Recitation**
From Aisyah radhiallahu’anha, she said:

> **أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ يَقُولُ فِي رُكُوعِهِ وَسُجُودِهِ، سُبُّوحٌ قُدُّوسٌ، رَبُّ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالرُّوحِ**
>
> *Subbuuhun quddus rabbul malaaikati war ruuh*
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say in his bowing and prostration: 'Subbuuhun quddus rabbul malaaikati war ruuh.'"
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 487)*

**Third Recitation**
From Ali bin Abi Talib radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **إِذَا سَجَدَ قَالَ: اللهُمَّ لَكَ سَجَدْتُ، وَبِكَ آمَنْتُ، وَلَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ، سَجَدَ وَجْهِي لِلَّذِي خَلَقَهُ وَصَوَّرَهُ، وَشَقَّ سَمْعَهُ وَبَصَرَهُ، تَبَارَكَ اللهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ**
>
> *Allahumma laka sajadtu, wa bika aamantu wa laka aslamtu...*
> "When the Prophet ﷺ prostrated he would say: 'Allahumma laka sajadtu... [O Allah, to You I have prostrated, in You I believe, and to You I submit. My face has prostrated to the One Who created it and shaped it, and opened its hearing and sight. Blessed is Allah, the Best of Creators]."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 771)*

items.title: Recommended to Make Abundant Dua
items.description: Sujud is the closest position to Allah, so it is recommended to make many supplications...
items.content_markdown:
### Recommended to Make Abundant Dua

After reciting the Sujud dhikr, it is recommended to make abundant supplications. The Prophet ﷺ said:

> **أَقَْربُ مَا يَكُوْنُ الْعَبْدِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ َوهُوَ سَاجِدً . فَأَكْثِرُوْا الدُعَا**
>
> "The nearest a servant comes to his Lord is when he is prostrating himself, so make supplication (in this state)."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 482)*

items.title: Prohibition of Reading Quran
items.description: Prohibition of reciting Quranic verses during Sujud...
items.content_markdown:
### Prohibition of Reading Quran

The Prophet ﷺ forbade reciting the Quran during Sujud:

> **نَهَانِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ رَاكِعًا أَوْ سَاجِدًا**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah forbade me to recite the Quran while bowing or prostrating."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 480)*

items.title: Rising From Sujud to Standing
items.description: Scholarly difference regarding how to rise from Sujud...
items.content_markdown:
### Rising From Sujud to Standing

Scholars differ into two opinions:

**1. Hands First (Hanafis & Hanbalis)**
Lifting both hands before the knees, unless there is difficulty.

From Jabir radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **رَمقْتُ ابنَ مَسعودٍ فرأيتُهُ يَنهَضُ علَى صدورِ قَدميهِ، ولا يَجلِسُ إذا صلَّى في أوَّلِ رَكْعةٍ حينَ يَقضي السُّجودَ**
>
> "I observed Ibn Mas'ud and saw him rising on the balls of his feet, and he did not sit (rest) in the first rak'ah when he finished sujud."
> *(Mushannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah)*

**2. Knees First (Shafi'is & Malikis)**
Lifting both knees before the hands.

items.title: Method of Sitting (Iftirasy)
items.description: The common way of sitting is Iftirasy, which is sitting on the left foot and keeping the right foot upright...
items.content_markdown:
### Method of Sitting Between Two Prostrations

The method of sitting between two prostrations is by **Iftirasy sitting**, which is by flattening the top of the left foot on the floor and sitting on it, then keeping the right foot upright with its toes facing the Qiblah.

From Abu Humaid As Sa’idi radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **فَإِذَا جَلَس فِي الرَكعَتَين جَلَس على رجلٌه اليسرى، ونصب اليمنى**
>
> "When the Prophet ﷺ sat in prayer in the first two rak'ahs, he sat on his left foot and kept his right foot upright."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 828 and Muslim no. 226)*

In another narration:

> **ثُمَّ ثَنَى رِجْلَهُ الْيُسْرَى وَقَعَدَ عَلَيْهَا ثُمَّ اعْتَدَلَ حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ كُلُّ عَظْمٍ فِى مَوْضِعِهِ مُعْتَدِلاً ثُمَّ أَهْوَى سَاجِدًا**
>
> "Then he bent his left leg and sat on it. Then he straightened up until every bone returned to its place properly. Then he went down for prostration."
> *(Narrated by Tirmidzi no. 304. At Tirmidzi said it is hasan sahih)*

items.title: Method of Iq'a Sitting
items.description: Besides Iftirasy, Iq'a sitting is also permissible with the correct method...
items.content_markdown:
### Iq’a Sitting

Besides Iftirasy sitting, **Iq’a sitting** is also permissible. The permissible method of Iq’a sitting in prayer is by keeping both feet upright and sitting on the heels of both feet, with the toes facing the Qiblah.

A Tabi'in, Thawus bin Kaisan rahimahullah said:

> **قُلنا لابنِ عباسٍ في الإقعاءِ على القدَمينِ . فقال : هي السنةُ . فقلنا له : إنا لنراهُ جفاءً بالرجلِ . فقال ابنُ عباسٍ : بل هي سنةُ نبيِّكَ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ**
>
> "We asked Ibn Abbas about Iq’a on the feet. He said: 'It is the Sunnah.' We said to him: 'We see it as harsh on the feet.' Ibn Abbas said: 'Rather, it is the Sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ.'"
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 536)*

**Prohibited Iq'a Sitting:**
The prohibited Iq’a sitting is placing the buttocks on the floor while the legs are spread out on the right and left sides of the body (like a dog sits). From Abu Hurairah radhiallahu’anhu:

> **وَنَهَانِي ... وَإِقْعَاءٍ كَإِقْعَاءِ الْكَلْبِ**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah... forbade me... from Iq'a sitting like the sitting of a dog."
> *(Narrated by Ahmad no. 8106)*

items.title: Supplications Between Two Prostrations
items.description: There are several authentic variations of supplications recited between two prostrations...
items.content_markdown:
### Supplications Recited Between Two Prostrations

There are several authentic supplications recited when sitting between two prostrations:

**First Recitation:**

> **رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَارْحَمْنِي وَاجْبُرْنِي وَارْزُقْنِي وَارْفَعْنِي**
>
> *Robbighfirlii warahmnii, wajburnii, warzuqnii, warfa’nii*
> (O Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, suffice me, grant me provision, and raise my rank)
> *(Narrated by Ibn Majah no.740, authenticated by Al Albani)*

**Second Recitation:**

> **اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَارْحَمْنِي وَاجْبُرْنِي وَاهْدِنِي وَارْزُقْنِي**
>
> *Allohummaghfirli warahmnii, wajburnii, wahdini, warzuqnii*
> (O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, suffice me, guide me, and grant me provision)
> *(Narrated by At Tirmidzi no.284, authenticated by Al Albani)*

**Third Recitation:**

> **اَللّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِيْ ، وَارْحَمْنِيْ ، وَعَافِنِيْ ، وَارْزُقْنِي**
>
> *Allahummaghfirlii warahmnii, wa’aafini, warzuqnii*
> (O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, grant me health, and grant me provision)
> *(Authenticated by Al Albani in Sahih At Targhib, 1562)*

**Fourth Recitation:**

> **رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي ، رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي**
>
> *Rabbighfirlii, rabbighfirlii*
> (O Lord, forgive me, O Lord, forgive me)
> *(Narrated by An Nasai no. 1665, authenticated by Al Albani)*
