items.title: Iftirasy Sitting Position
items.description: The sitting position for the first Tashahhud is Iftirasy...
items.content_markdown:
### Iftirasy Sitting Position

The method of sitting for the first Tashahhud is **Iftirasy Sitting**, which is sitting on the spread-out left foot and keeping the right foot upright. The right hand is placed on the right thigh/knee, and the left hand on the left thigh/knee.

As in the Hadith from Abu Humaid As Sa’idi radhiallahu’anhu:

> **فإذا جلس في الركعتين جلس على رجلٌه اليسرى، ونصب اليمنى**
>
> "When the Prophet ﷺ sat in prayer in the first two rak'ahs, he sat on his left foot and kept his right foot upright."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 828 and Muslim no. 226)*

Also the Prophet's ﷺ saying:

> **فَإِذَا جَلَسْتَ فِي وَسَطِ الصَّلَاةِ فَاطْمَئِنَّ، وَافْتَرِشْ فَخِذَكَ الْيُسْرَى ثُمَّ تَشَهَّدْ**
>
> "When you sit in the middle of the prayer (first Tashahhud), sit calmly, flatten your left thigh (sit Iftirasy), then perform Tashahhud."
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud no. 860, authenticated by Al Albani)*

items.title: Pointing with Index Finger
items.description: It is Sunnah to point with the right index finger towards the Qiblah...
items.content_markdown:
### Pointing with Index Finger

It is Sunnah to point with the right index finger towards the Qiblah, and the gaze should be fixed on the pointing finger.

In the Hadith of Abdullah bin Umar radhiallahu’anhu:

> **أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ إِذَا جَلَسَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَضَعَ يَدَيْهِ عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ ، وَرَفَعَ إِصْبَعَهُ الْيُمْنَى الَّتِي تَلِي الْإِبْهَامَ ، فَدَعَا بِهَا ، وَيَدُهُ الْيُسْرَى عَلَى رُكْبَتِهِ بَاسِطُهَا عَلَيْهَا**
>
> "When the Prophet ﷺ sat in prayer, he placed his hands on his knees and raised his right finger, which is next to the thumb (the index finger), and supplicated with it. And his left hand was on his knee, spread out upon it."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 580)*

It is recommended to point from the very beginning of the sitting of Tashahhud until the end, based on the general meaning of the hadith above: *"When the Prophet ﷺ sat in prayer... he raised his right finger"*.

Shaykh Abdul Aziz bin Baz said:

> **ويشير بالسبabaة من حين يجلس إلى أن يسلم**
>
> "And he points with the index finger from the moment he sits until he performs Taslim."
> *(Fatawa Nurun ‘alad Darbi)*

items.title: Tashahhud Recitations
items.description: There are three authentic variations of Tashahhud recitations from the Prophet ﷺ...
items.content_markdown:
### Tashahhud Recitations

There are three authentic variations of the first Tashahhud recitation from the Prophet ﷺ:

**First Recitation (Ibn Mas'ud Narration)**

From Ibn Mas'ud radhiallahu’anhu, he said the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught:

> **التَّحِيَاتُ لِلَّهِ وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللهِ الصَّالِحِيْنَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُوْلُهُ**
>
> *At tahiyyaatu lillaah was shalawaatu wat thayyibaatu. As salaamu ‘alaika ayyuhannabiyyu warahmatullah wabarakaatuh. As salaamu ‘alainaa wa ‘ala ibaadillahis shaalihiin. Asyhadu an laailaaha illallah, wa asy-hadu anna muhammadan abduhu wara suuluh*
>
> (All compliments, prayers, and pure words are due to Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger).
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 1202, Muslim no. 402)*

**Second Recitation (Ibn Abbas Narration)**

From Ibn Abbas radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **اَلتَّحِيَاتُ المُبَارَكَاتُ، الصَلَوَاتُ الطَّيِّبَاتُ لله، اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَينَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللهِ الصَالِحِين، أَشْهَدُ أَن لَّا إِلَهَ إِلّا الله، وَأَشْهَدُ أنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُوْلُ الله**
>
> *At tahiyaatu mubaarokaatu sholawaatu thoyyibaatu lillah, Assalamu ‘alaika ayyuhannabiyyu wa rohmatullahi wabarokaatuh, Assalamu’alainaa wa ‘alaa ‘ibaadillahi shoolihiin, Asyhadu allaa ilaaha illallaah, wa asyhadu anna muhammadan rasuulullah.*
>
> (All blessed compliments, prayers, and pure words are due to Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger).
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 403)*

items.title: Moving the Index Finger?
items.description: Explanation regarding the difference of opinion on whether to move the index finger or keep it still...
items.content_markdown:
### Moving the Index Finger?

In the Hadith of Wail bin Hujr radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **... ثُمَّ قَبَضَ اثْنَتَيْنِ مِنْ أَصَابِعِهِ وَحَلَّقَ حَلْقَةً ثُمَّ رَفَعَ إِصْبَعَهُ فَرَأَيْتُهُ يُحَرِّكُهَا يَدْعُو بِهَا**
>
> "...Then he clenched two of his fingers (pinky and ring), formed a circle with two fingers (thumb and middle), and pointed with his index finger, and I saw him moving it while supplicating with it."
> *(Narrated by An Nasai no. 888)*

**Scholarly Difference of Opinion:**

1.  **Not Moving (Still)**
    Many scholars (such as Shaykh Muqbil, Shaykh Shu'aib Al Arnauth) consider the additional phrase *"I saw him moving it"* to be **syadz** (weak/odd) because it is only narrated by Zaidah bin Qudamah, whereas 12 other trustworthy narrators did not mention the movement.

2.  **Moving**
    Some other scholars (such as Shaykh Al Albani) consider the narration authentic, thus prescribing moving the finger when supplicating in Tashahhud.

**Conclusion (Rajih):**
The more correct view (*rajih*), wallahu a’lam, is that the addition is *syadz* and therefore *dha’if* (weak). Thus, one does not need to move the index finger during Tashahhud.

However, this is a matter of acceptable scholarly difference (*khilafiyah ijtihadiyyah*) among scholars, and we should be flexible towards the opinion that prescribes moving the finger.

items.title: Method of Sitting for Final Tashahhud
items.description: The method of sitting for the final Tashahhud is by Tawarruk...
items.content_markdown:
### Method of Sitting for Final Tashahhud

The method of sitting for the final Tashahhud is by **Tawarruk** sitting, which is sitting on the floor, placing both feet to the right side of the waist, spreading the left foot, while keeping the right foot upright.

In the Hadith of Abu Humaid As Sa’idi radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **فإذا جلس في الركعتين جلس على رجلٌه اليسرى، ونصب اليمنى، وإذا جلس في الركعة الآخرة، قدم رجلٌه اليسرى، ونصب الأخرى، وقعد على مقعدته**
>
> "When the Prophet ﷺ sat in prayer in the first two rak'ahs, he sat on his left foot and kept his right foot upright. When he sat in the last rak'ah, he pushed out his left foot and kept the other upright, and sat on his buttocks."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 828 and Muslim no. 226)*

In another narration:

> **حتَّى إذا كانتِ الرَّكعةُ التي تنقضي فيها الصَّلاةُ، أخَّرَ رِجْلَه اليُسرى، وقعَد على شِقِّه متورِّكًا ثم سلَّمَ**
>
> "When the Prophet ﷺ reached the last rak'ah (which ends the prayer), he pushed out his left foot and sat on his hip (Tawarruk), then he performed Taslim."
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud no. 730, authenticated by Al Albani in Sahih Abu Daud)*

Similarly, if there are two Tashahhuds in the prayer, then the first Tashahhud is recited in the Iftirasy sitting position and the second Tashahhud is recited in the Tawarruk sitting position as per the apparent meaning (*zahir*) of the Hadiths above.

### Method of Sitting if There is Only One Tashahhud

Scholars differ (*khilaf*) regarding the method of sitting for the final Tashahhud if there is only one Tashahhud in the prayer. Because in the Hadith of Abu Humaid above, there is an indication that the Prophet sat in Iftirasy in the second rak'ah, whereas in the narration of Abu Daud it is understood that Tawarruk sitting is for the Tashahhud in the last rak'ah. Yet if the prayer is only two rak'ahs, then the sitting for Tashahhud is the Tashahhud in the second rak'ah as well as in the last rak'ah.

Scholars have two opinions:

**First Opinion: Sitting in Tawarruk.**
This is the opinion of the Shafi'is and Malikis. Their evidence is the narration of Abu Humaid which contains the wording:

> **حتَّى إذا كانتِ الرَّكعةُ التي تنقضي فيها الصَّلاةُ، أخَّرَ رِجْلَه اليُسرى، وقعَد على شِقِّه متورِّكًا ثم سلَّمَ**
>
> "When the Prophet ﷺ reached the last rak'ah (which ends the prayer), he pushed out his left foot and sat on his hip (Tawarruk), then he performed Taslim."

**Second Opinion: Sitting in Iftirasy.**
This is the opinion of the Hanbalis and Hanafis, also supported by Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih Al Utsaimin and Shaykh Abdul Aziz bin Baz. Their evidence is the Hadith of Abu Humaid narrated by Bukhari – Muslim above:

> **فإذا جلس في الركعتين جلس على رجلٌه اليسرى، ونصب اليمنى**
>
> "When the Prophet ﷺ sat in prayer in the first two rak'ahs, he sat on his left foot and kept his right foot upright."

Supported by the narration of Aisyah radhiallahu’anha:

> **وكان يقولُ في كلِّ ركعتين التحيةَ، وكان يفرشُ رِجلَه اليُسرَى، وينصبُ رِجلَه اليُمنَى**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ used to say the Tahiyyah (Tashahhud) in every two rak'ahs. And he would spread his left foot and keep his right foot upright."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 498)*

**Thus, the second opinion seems to be the more correct (*rajih*), wallahu a’lam.**

items.title: Ruling of Salawat in Final Tashahhud
items.description: Differences of opinion regarding the ruling of Salawat in the final Tashahhud...
items.content_markdown:
### Salawat in Final Tashahhud

Scholars differ regarding its ruling into two opinions:

**First Opinion: It is Sunnah.**
This is the opinion of the Hanafis, Malikis, Ibn Abdil Barr, Ibnul Munzhir, the Zahiris, and also the opinion supported by Shaykh Muhammad bin Salih Al Utsaimin.

The evidence they use is a Hadith from Alqamah:

> **عَلقمةَ أنَّ عبدَ اللهِ بنَ مسعودٍ أخذَ بيدِه، وأنَّ رسولَ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم أخَذ بيدِ عبدِ اللهِ فعلَّمَه التشهُّدَ في الصَّلاةِ ... قال: فإذا قضَيْتَ هذا أو قال: فإذا فعَلْتَ هذا، فقد قضَيْتَ صلاتَك، إن شئتَ أنْ تقومَ فقُمْ، وإن شِئْتَ أنْ تقعُدَ فاقعُدْ**
>
> "Abdullah bin Mas'ud took Alqamah's hand, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took Ibn Mas'ud's hand to teach him the Tashahhud in prayer... The Prophet then said: 'If you have finished saying this, then you have completed your prayer. If you wish to stand, then stand, or if you wish to sit, then sit.'"
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud no. 970)*

However, Shaykh Al Albani asserted:

> **شاذّ بزيادة ((إذا قلت..))، والصواب أنَّه من قول ابن مسعود موقوفًا عليه**
>
> "This Hadith is *syadz* (weak/odd) with the addition: 'if you have said this, etc.' The correct view is that this is a *mauquf* narration, representing the words of Ibn Mas'ud."
> *(Sahih Sunan Abu Daud no. 970)*

**Second Opinion: It is Obligatory.**
This is the opinion of the Hanbalis, Shafi'is, Ibn Arabi, and supported by Shaykh Abdul Aziz bin Baz.

Their evidence is the Hadith of Ka’ab bin Ujrah radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **إنَّ النبيَّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم خرَج علينا، فقُلْنا: يا رسولَ اللهِ، قد علِمْنا كيف نُسلِّمُ عليك، فكيف نُصلِّي عليك؟ قال: قولوا: اللهمَّ صلِّ على محمَّدٍ، وعلى آلِ محمَّدٍ، كما صلَّيْتَ على آلِ إبراهيمَ، إنَّك حميدٌ مجيدٌ، اللهمَّ بارِكْ على محمَّدٍ، وعلى آلِ محمَّدٍ، كما بارَكْتَ على آلِ إبراهيمَ، إنَّك حميدٌ مجيدٌ**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ came out to us, and we said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we know how to greet you, but how should we send blessings upon you?' The Prophet replied: 'Say:
> **Allahumma shalli ‘ala Muhammad wa ‘ala aali Muhammad kamaa shalayta ‘ala aali Ibrahim, innaka hamiidum majiid. Allahumma baarik ‘ala Muhammad wa ‘ala aali Muhamamd kamaa baarakta ‘ala aali Ibrahim, innaka hamiidum majid**'
> (O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious)"
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 6357, Muslim no. 406)*

In this Hadith, the imperative form (*fi’il amr*) is used, indicating that it is obligatory. **Wallahu a’lam, this opinion is more correct (*rajih*).**

items.title: Reciting Protection from Four Things
items.description: It is recommended to recite protection from four things before Taslim...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting Protection from Four Things

After the final Tashahhud and before Taslim, it is recommended to recite protection from four things. From Abu Hurairah radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet ﷺ said:

> **إذا فرَغَ أحَدُكم مِن التشهُّدِ الآخِرِ، فلْيتعوَّذْ باللهِ مِن أربعٍ: يقولُ : اللهم ! إني أعوذُ بك من عذابِ جهنمَ . ومن عذابِ القبرِ . ومن فتنةِ المحيا والمماتِ . ومن شرِّ فتنةِ المسيحِ الدجالِ**
>
> "When one of you finishes the final Tashahhud, he should seek refuge in Allah from four things, saying:
> **'Allahumma inni a’udzubika min ‘adzabi jahannam, wamin ‘adzabil qabri, wamin fitnatil mahyaa wal mamaat, wamin syarri fitnatil masiihid dajjaal'**
> (O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the False Messiah / Al Masih Ad Dajjal)."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 588)*

items.title: Ruling of the Second Salam
items.description: Scholars differ regarding the ruling of the second Taslim into two opinions...
items.content_markdown:
### Ruling of the Second Salam

Scholars differ regarding the ruling of the second Taslim into two opinions:

**First Opinion: It is Sunnah.**
This is the opinion of the majority of scholars (Jumhur) and even consensus (ijma) has been reported from some scholars, as cited by An-Nawawi above. Consensus is also reported by Ibn Abdil Barr, Al-Qurthubi, At-Thahawi, and Ibn Rajab.

Among the evidences is the Hadith from Aisyah radhiallahu’anha, she said:

> **كان رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم إذا أوتَرَ بتسعِ ركعاتٍ لم يقعُدْ إلَّا في الثامنةِ، فيحمَدُ اللهَ ويذكُرُه ويدعو ثم ينهَضُ ولا يُسلِّمُ، ثم يُصلِّي التاسعةَ، فيجلِسُ فيذكُرُ اللهَ عزَّ وجلَّ ويدعو ويسلِّمُ تسليمةً يُسمِعُنا، ثم يُصلِّي ركعتينِ وهو جالسٌ، فلمَّا كبِرَ وضعُفَ أوتَرَ بسبعِ ركعاتٍ لا يقعُدُ إلَّا في السادسةِ، ثم ينهَضُ ولا يُسلِّمُ ثم يُصلِّي السابعةَ، ثم يُسلِّمُ تسليمةً، ثم يُصلِّي ركعتينِ وهو جالسٌ، ثم يُسلِّمُ تسليمةً واحدةً: السَّلامُ عليكم، يرفَعُ بها صوتَه حتَّى يوقِظَنا**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Witr with nine rak'ahs, in which he would not sit except in the eighth. He would praise Allah, remember Him, and supplicate, then he would get up without saying Salam. Then he would pray the ninth rak'ah, sit, remember Allah 'Azza wa Jalla, supplicate, and then say Salam with one Taslim that he made us hear. When he grew old and weak, he prayed Witr with seven rak'ahs, in which he would not sit except in the sixth. Then he would get up without saying Salam. Then he would pray the seventh rak'ah, then say Salam with one Taslim. Then he would pray another two rak'ahs while sitting, then he performed Salam with one Taslim, saying: **assalamu’alaikum**. He raised his voice with it until he woke us up."
> *(Narrated by An Nasai 3/240, authenticated by Al Albani in Sahih An Nasai)*

In this Hadith, the Prophet ﷺ is mentioned to have performed Salam only once, indicating that the second Salam is not obligatory.

This opinion is also the opinion of the majority of the Prophet's companions and the Salaf generation. From Nafi’, he said regarding Ibn Umar radhiallahu’anhu:

> **أنه كان يسلم عن يمينه واحدة**
>
> "That Ibnu Umar used to say Salam to his right only once."
> *(Narrated by Abdurrazzaq in Al Mushannaf, 2/222. Its chain is Sahih)*

There are also reports from Aisyah, Ali bin Abi Talib, Salamah bin Al-Akwa’, and Anas bin Malik radhiallahu’anhum that they also performed Salam only once.

**Second Opinion: It is Obligatory.**
This is the opinion of the Hanbalis. Their evidence is the Hadith from Jabir bin Samurah radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet ﷺ said:

> **إنَّما يكفي أحدَكم أنْ يضَعَ يدَه على فخِذِه، ثم يُسلِّمَ على أخيه مِن على يمينِه وشِمالِه**
>
> "It suffices one of you to place his hand on his thigh, then say Salam to his brother to his right and to his left."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 431)*

In this Hadith, the word *yakfi* (suffices) is used, implying that the Salam is only sufficient if done to the right and left.

**Wallahu a’lam, the majority opinion is more correct (*rajih*) in this matter**, considering the many reports of consensus and narrations from the Salaf. As for the deduction from the Hadith of Jabir bin Samurah, it is not explicit (*sharih*).

items.title: Method of Performing Salam
items.description: Salam is performed by turning to the right until the cheek is visible from behind...
items.content_markdown:
### Method of Performing Salam

Salam is performed by turning to the right until the cheek is visible from behind, then turning to the left until the cheek is visible from behind, while saying the Salam.

As in the Hadith from Ibn Mas'ud radhiallahu’anhu:

> **أنَّ النبيَّ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم كان يُسلِّمُ عن يمينِه وعن يسارِه: السَّلامُ عليكم ورحمةُ اللهِ، السَّلامُ عليكم ورحمةُ اللهِ حتَّى يُرَى بَياضُ خَدِّه**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ used to say Salam to his right and to his left: **as salaamu ‘alaikum warahmatullah** (to the right), **as salaamu ‘alaikum warahmatullah** (to the left), until the whiteness of his cheek was visible."
> *(Narrated by Abu Daud no. 996, Ibn Majah no. 914, authenticated by Al Albani in Sahih Ibn Majah)*

Also in the Hadith from Amir bin Sa’ad radhiallahu’anhu:

> **كنتُ أرى رسولَ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّم يُسلِّمُ عن يمينِه، وعن يسارِه، حتَّى أرى بَياضَ خَدِّه**
>
> "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performing Taslim to his right and to his left, until I saw the whiteness of his cheek."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 582)*

items.title: Recitations of Salam
items.description: There are several authentic recitations of Salam from the Prophet ﷺ...
items.content_markdown:
### Recitations of Salam

There are several authentic recitations of Salam from the Prophet ﷺ:

**First: assalamu’alaikum**
As in the Hadith of Aisyah radhiallahu’anha above.

**Second: assalamu’alaikum warahmatullah**
As in the Hadith of Ibn Mas'ud above. Also in the narration from Ibn Umar radhiallahu’anhu, he said:

> **يقول : السلام عليكم ورحمة الله عن يمينه ، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله عن يساره**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ used to say: **assalamu’alaikum warahmatullah** to his right and **assalamu’alaikum warahmatullah** to his left."
> *(Narrated by An Nasai no. 1319, authenticated by Al Albani in Sahih An Nasai)*

**Third: assalamu’alaikum warahmatullah to the right and as salamu’alaikum to the left**
As in another narration from Ibn Umar radhiallahu’anhu, from Wasi’ bin Hibban he said:

> **قلتُ لابنِ عمرَ : أخبِرني عن صلاةِ رسولِ اللَّهِ صلَّى اللَّهُ عليْهِ وسلَّمَ كيفَ كانت ؟ قالَ : فذَكرَ التَّكبيرَ – قالَ : – يعني – وذَكرَ السَّلامُ عليكُم ورحمةُ اللَّهِ عن يمينِهِ السَّلامُ عليكم عن يسارِه**
>
> "I said to Ibn Umar: Tell me about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ... He mentioned that the Prophet's Salam was **assalamu’alaikum warahmatullah** to his right and **assalamu’alaikum** to his left."
> *(Narrated by An Nasai no. 1320, authenticated by Al Albani in Sahih An Nasai)*

As for the greeting with the addition of “wa barakatuhu”, it is a *syadz* (weak/odd) narration. Shaykh Abdul Aziz Ath Tharifi said:

> **و أما زيادة وبركاته فلا أصل له. جاء في نسخة عند أبي داود, و يظهر أنها من بعض النساخ, وليست في الرواية أصلا, و إن كانت في الرواية فهي شاذة**
>
> "As for the addition of **wa barakatuhu**, it has no basis. It appears in a manuscript of Abu Daud, and it seems to be an insertion from some copyists, not originally in the narration. Even if it were in the narration, it is *syadz*."
> *(Sifatu Shalatin Nabi, 147)*

title: Tuma’ninah (Tranquility) in Prayer
description: A collection of evidences commanding tuma'ninah and perfecting ruku' and sujud.

items.title: Command to Perfect Ruku' and Sujud
items.description: The Prophet ﷺ commanded to perfect ruku' and sujud with tuma'ninah...
items.content_markdown:
### Command to Perfect Ruku' and Sujud

There are very many Hadiths of the Prophet that command to establish and perfect the prayer and warn to be careful if one is not tuma'ninah in prayer.

**First**, a hadith narrated by Imam Bukhari and Imam Muslim from the companion Anas bin Malik radhiallahu ‘anhu, that the Prophet shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam said,

> **أَتِمُّوا الرُّكُوعَ وَالسُّجُودَ**
>
> “Perfect the ruku’ and sujud”
> *(HR Bukhari 6644 and Muslim 4525)*

What is meant by perfecting, must be with tuma'ninah (calmness).

items.title: Prayer Invalid Without Straightening Back
items.description: Hadith of Ali bin Syaiban regarding the invalidity of prayer for those who do not straighten their backs...
items.content_markdown:
### Prayer Invalid Without Straightening Back

**Second**, a hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Majah with a sahih chain from Ali bin Syaiban who said, “We once prayed behind the Messenger of Allah shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam, then he glanced at a man whose prayer was not upright (i.e., did not straighten his spine) in ruku and sujud. When the prayer was finished, the Prophet shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam said:

> **يا معشر المسلمين  لاَ صَلاَةَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يُقِمْ صُلْبَهُ فِى الرُّكُوْعِ والسُّجُوْدِ**
>
> “O assembly of Muslims, there is no prayer for those who do not straighten their backs when ruku’ and sujud’”
> *(HR Ahmad 16297, Ibn Majah 871 and authenticated by Al Albani in Shahihul Jami’ 7977)*

That is, not straightening his spine when ruku’ and sujud. This hadith is evidence that standing, sitting, and tuma'ninah are pillars in sujud and prayer.

items.title: Prohibition of Pecking Like a Chicken
items.description: Severe threat for those who pray quickly without tuma'ninah...
items.content_markdown:
### Prohibition of Pecking Like a Chicken

**Third**, Abu Ya’la narrated in his Musnad with a hasan chain, that the Prophet shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam saw a man who was praying but did not perfect his ruku’ and was like a chicken pecking in his sujud (because of the quickness of his sujud). So he said,

> **لَوْ مَاتَ هَذَا عَلَى ما هو عليه مَاتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ مِلَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ**
>
> “If this person dies in such a condition of prayer, then he dies not on the religion of Muhammad”
> *(Musnad Abu Ya’la No 7184, narrated by Ath Thabrani in Al Kabiir No 3840, basaned by Al Albani in Shifat ash Shalah page 131)*

This is a very severe threat, the person who does such an act is feared to die in a state of suul khaitmah (bad ending), dying not upon Islam, wal’iyadzubillah.

items.title: Three Prohibitions in Prayer
items.description: Prohibition of pecking like a chicken, sitting like a dog, and turning like a fox...
items.content_markdown:
### Three Prohibitions in Prayer

**Fourth**, Imam Ahmad and others narrated a hadith from Abu Hurairah radhiallahu ‘anhu who said, “The Messenger of Allah shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam commanded me 3 things and forbade me 3 things:

> **ونَهَانِي عَنْ نَقْرَةٍ كَنَقْرَةِ الدِّيكِ، وإِقْعَاءٍ كَإِقْعَاءِ الكَلْبِ، والْتِفَاتٍ كَالْتِفَاتِ الثَّعْلَبِ**
>
> He forbade me from pecking like the pecking of a rooster, sitting like the sitting of a dog, and turning like the turning of a fox”
> *(HR Ahmad 8106, Hasaned by Shaykh al Albani in Shahih at Targhib 555)*

items.title: Threat of Dying Not on the Sunnah
items.description: Hudzaifah bin Yaman's warning to one whose ruku' and sujud were not perfect...
items.content_markdown:
### Threat of Dying Not on the Sunnah

**Fifth**, a hadith narrated by Imam Bukhari in Shahih Bukhari, that one time Hudzaifah bin Yaman saw someone whose ruku’ and sujud were not perfect. When this person finished praying, Hudzaifah said to him, “Prayer like that?” then apparently Hudzaifah said,

> “If you were to die, you would die not upon the sunnah of Muhammad shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam”

In another narration,

> “If you were to die, you would die not upon the fitrah that Allah has created for Muhammad shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam”
> *(Narrated by Imam Bukhari in Shahih Bukhari 791)*

items.title: Allah Does Not Look at Prayer Without Tuma'ninah
items.description: Allah will not look at the prayer of a servant who does not straighten his spine...
items.content_markdown:
### Allah Does Not Look at Prayer Without Tuma'ninah

**Sixth**, a hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and others from the companion Thalaq bin Ali radhiallahu ‘anhu, he said, the Prophet shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam once said:

> **لَا يَنْظُرُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِلَى صَلَاةِ عَبْدٍ لَا يُقِيمُ فِيهَا صُلْبَهُ بَيْنَ رُكُوعِهَا وَسُجُودِهَا**
>
> “Allah will not look at a servant who does not straighten his spine between his ruku’ and his sujud”
> *(HR Ahmad 16283, Al Albani considered the chain good in Ash Shahihah 2536)*

items.title: Prophet's Guidance: Standing and Sitting Upright
items.description: The Prophet did not go down for sujud until he stood up completely, and did not sujud again until he sat upright...
items.content_markdown:
### Prophet's Guidance: Standing and Sitting Upright

**Seventh**, Imam Muslim narrated in Shahih Muslim from Aisyah radhiallahu ‘anha, she said,

> “The Prophet shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam used to, when he raised from ruku’, he would not go down for sujud until he really stood up. And when he raised from sujud, he would not sujud again until he really sat upright”
> *(Narrated by Imam Muslim in Shahih Muslim 498)*

title: Dhikr After Prayer
description: A collection of authentic Dhikr recited after obligatory prayers.

items.title: Istighfar and Supplication for Peace
items.description: Reciting Istighfar 3x followed by the supplication Allahumma antas salam...
items.content_markdown:
### Istighfar 3x, and reading the supplication “Allahumma antas salam…”

From Thawban radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet ﷺ said,

> **كانَ رَسولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عليه وسلَّمَ، إذَا انْصَرَفَ مِن صَلَاتِهِ اسْتَغْفَرَ ثَلَاثًا وَقالَ: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلَامُ وَمِنْكَ السَّلَامُ، تَبَارَكْتَ ذَا الجَلَالِ وَالإِكْرَامِ**
>
> "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he would ask for forgiveness (Istighfar) 3 times, then say:
> **Alloohumma antas salaam wa minkas salaam tabaarokta yaa dzal jalaali wal ikroom**
> (O Allah, You represent peace, and peace comes only from You. Blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor)."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 591)*

items.title: Tahlil and Supplication Laa Maani'a
items.description: Reciting Tahlil and the supplication Allahumma laa maani’a lima a’thayta...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting Tahlil and supplication “Allahumma laa maani’a lima a’thayta…”

From Al Mughirah bin Shu’bah radhiallahu’anhu, he said,

> **سَمِعْتُ النبيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ يقولُ خَلْفَ الصَّلَاةِ: لا إلَهَ إلَّا اللَّهُ وحْدَهُ لا شَرِيكَ له، اللَّهُمَّ لا مَانِعَ لِما أعْطَيْتَ، ولَا مُعْطِيَ لِما مَنَعْتَ، ولَا يَنْفَعُ ذَا الجَدِّ مِنْكَ الجَدُّ**
>
> "I heard the Prophet ﷺ saying after the prayer:
> **laa ilaha illallooh wahdahu laa syarika lahu, lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu wa huwa ‘alaa kulli syai-in qodiir. Alloohumma laa maani’a lima a’thoyta wa laa mu’thiya limaa mana’ta wa laa yanfa’u dzal jaddi minkal jaddu**
> (There is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the Dominion, and to Him belongs all Praise, and He is Able to do all things. O Allah, there is none who can withhold what You give, and none who can give what You withhold; and the wealth/glory of the wealthy/glorious is of no avail against You)."
> *(Narrated by Bukhari no. 6615, Muslim no. 593)*

items.title: Tahlil Narration of Abdullah bin Zubair
items.description: Complete Tahlil recitation usually recited by Abdullah bin Zubair at the end of prayer...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting supplication “Laa ilaha illallah wahdahu laa syarika lahu…”

As in the narration from Abdullah bin Zubair radhiallahu’anhu,

> **كانَ ابنُ الزُّبَيْرِ يقولُ: في دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ حِينَ يُسَلِّمُ لا إلَهَ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لا شَرِيكَ له، له المُلْكُ وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ وَهو علَى كُلِّ شيءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إلَّا باللَّهِ، لا إلَهَ إلَّا اللَّهُ، وَلَا نَعْبُدُ إلَّا إيَّاهُ، له النِّعْمَةُ وَلَهُ الفَضْلُ، وَلَهُ الثَّنَاءُ الحَسَنُ، لا إلَهَ إلَّا اللَّهُ مُخْلِصِينَ له الدِّينَ ولو كَرِهَ الكَافِرُونَ وَقالَ: كانَ رَسولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عليه وسلَّمَ يُهَلِّلُ بهِنَّ دُبُرَ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ**
>
> Abdullah bin Zubair used to say at the end of every prayer, after performing Taslim:
> **laa ilaha illalloohu wahdahu laa syarika lahu. Lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu wa huwa ‘alaa kulli syai-in qodiir. Laa haula wa laa quwwata illa billaah. Laa ilaha illallooh wa laa na’budu illa iyyaah. Lahun ni’matu wa lahul fadhlu wa lahuts tsanaa-ul hasanu. Laa ilaha illallooh mukhlishiina lahud diin wa lau karihal kaafiruun**
> (There is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the Dominion, and to Him belongs all Praise, and He is Able to do all things. There is no power and no strength except with Allah. There is no god worthy of worship except Allah, and we worship none but Him. To Him belong the bounties, the grace, and the good praise. There is no god worthy of worship except Allah, we are sincere to Him in religion, although the disbelievers dislike it)."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 594)*

items.title: Tasbih, Tahmid, Takbir, and Tahlil
items.description: Four authentic forms of Tasbih, Tahmid, Takbir, and Tahlil recitations...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting Tasbih, Tahmid, Takbir, and Tahlil

Regarding the recitation of Tasbih, Tahmid, Takbir, and Tahlil after prayer, there are 4 authentic forms from the Prophet ﷺ:

**1. Tasbih 33x, Tahmid 33x, Takbir 33x, Tahlil 1x, total 100 dhikr**

As in the narration from Abu Hurairah radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet ﷺ said,

> **مَنْ سَبَّحَ اللهَ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ ثَلَاثًا وَثَلَاثِينَ ، وَحَمِدَ اللهَ ثَلَاثًا وَثَلَاثِينَ ، وَكَبَّرَ اللهَ ثَلَاثًا وَثَلَاثِينَ ، فَتْلِكَ تِسْعَةٌ وَتِسْعُونَ ، وَقَالَ تَمَامَ الْمِائَةِ : لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ غُفِرَتْ خَطَايَاهُ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِثْلَ زَبَدِ الْبَحْرِ**
>
> "Whoever glorifies Allah (Tasbih) after every prayer 33 times, praises Allah (Tahmid) 33 times, and magnifies Allah (Takbir) 33 times, making ninety-nine, and completes one hundred by saying:
> **Subhanallah wal hamdulillah wallahu akbar (33 x). Laa ilaha illallah wahda, laa syarika lah. Lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu wa huwa ‘ala kulli syai-in qodiir**
> (Glory be to Allah, Praise be to Allah, Allah is the Greatest (33x). There is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone. There is no partner for Him. To Him belongs the Dominion and to Him belongs the Praise, and He is Able to do all things)
> Then his sins will be forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 597)*

**2. Tasbih 33x, Tahmid 33x, Takbir 34x, total 100 dhikr**

As in the narration from Ka’ab bin Ujrah radhiallahu’anhu, from the Prophet ﷺ,

> **مُعَقِّبَاتٌ لَا يَخِيبُ قَائِلُهُنَّ – أَوْ فَاعِلُهُنَّ – دُبُرَ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ ، ثَلَاثٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ تَسْبِيحَةً ، وَثَلَاثٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ تَحْمِيدَةً ، وَأَرْبَعٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً**
>
> "There are successors (dhikrs) relating to which the one who says them – or does them – after every obligatory prayer will not be disappointed: 33 Tasbih, 33 Tahmid, and 34 Takbir."
> *(Narrated by Muslim no. 596)*

**3. Tasbih 25x, Tahmid 25x, Takbir 25x, Tahlil 25x, total 100 dhikr**

As in the narration from Zaid bin Tsabit radhiallahu’anhu, he said,

> **أُمِرُوا أَنْ يُسَبِّحُوا دُبُرَ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ ثَلَاثًا وَثَلَاثِينَ ، وَيَحْمَدُوا ثَلَاثًا وَثَلَاثِينَ ، وَيُكَبِّرُوا أَرْبَعًا وَثَلَاثِينَ ، فَأُتِيَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ فِي مَنَامِهِ ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ : أَمَرَكُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ تُسَبِّحُوا دُبُرَ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ ثَلَاثًا وَثَلَاثِينَ ، وَتَحْمَدُوا ثَلَاثًا وَثَلَاثِينَ ، وَتُكَبِّرُوا أَرْبَعًا وَثَلَاثِينَ ؟ قَالَ : نَعَمْ ، قَالَ : فَاجْعَلُوهَا خَمْسًا وَعِشْرِينَ ، وَاجْعَلُوا فِيهَا التَّهْلِيلَ ، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَذَكَرَ ذَلِكَ لَهُ ، فَقَالَ: ( اجْعَلُوهَا كَذَلِكَ )**
>
> "They (the companions) were commanded to recite Tasbih after prayer 33 times, Tahmid 33 times, and Takbir 34 times. Then a man from the Ansar had a dream... The person in the dream said: Make them all 25 times and add Tahlil. When he woke up in the morning, this Ansari man went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned his dream. The Prophet said: Do it like that!"
> *(Narrated by An Nasai no. 1350, authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih An Nasai)*

**4. Tasbih 10x, Tahmid 10x, Takbir 10x, total 30 dhikr**

As in the narration from Abdullah bin Amr radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet ﷺ said,

> **خصلتان ، أو خلتان لا يحافظ عليهما عبد مسلم إلا دخل الجنة ، هما يسير ، ومن يعمل بهما قليل ، يسبح في دبر كل صلاة عشرا ، ويحمد عشرا ، ويكبر عشرا ، فذلك خمسون ومائة بًاللسان ، وألف وخمسمائة في الميزان**
>
> "There are two qualities which, if a Muslim servant maintains them, he will certainly enter Paradise. They are easy, but those who practice them are few. (First) Glorifying Allah (Tasbih) after every prayer 10 times, Praising Him (Tahmid) 10 times, and Magnifying Him (Takbir) 10 times. That is 150 dhikrs on the tongue (in 5 prayers) but 1500 in the scales..."
> *(Narrated by Abu Dawud no. 5065, authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud)*

items.title: Reciting Ayat Kursi
items.description: The virtue of reciting Ayat Kursi after every obligatory prayer...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting Ayat Kursi

As in the Hadith from Abu Umamah Al Bahili radhiallahu’anhu, the Prophet ﷺ said,

> **مَن قرأَ آيةَ الكرسيِّ دبُرَ كلِّ صلاةٍ مَكْتوبةٍ ، لم يمنَعهُ مِن دخولِ الجنَّةِ ، إلَّا الموتُ**
>
> "Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, nothing will prevent him from entering Paradise except death."
> *(Narrated by An Nasai no. 9928, At-Thabrani no. 7532, authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Al-Jami’ no. 6464)*

items.title: Reciting Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Naas
items.description: Command to read Al Mu'awwidzat at the end of every prayer...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Naas

As in the Hadith from Uqbah bin ‘Amir radhiallahu’anhu, he said,

> **أمرني رسولُ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ أن أقرأَ بالمُعوِّذاتِ دُبُرَ كلِّ صلاةٍ**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to recite Al-Mu'awwidzat (An-Naas, Al-Falaq, Al-Ikhlas) at the end of every prayer."
> *(Narrated by Abu Dawud no. 1523, authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abu Dawud)*

items.title: Supplication for Beneficial Knowledge (Fajr)
items.description: Specific supplication recited by the Prophet after Fajr Salam...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting supplication “Allahumma inni as-aluka ilman naafi’an…”

From Umm Salamah Hindun bint Abi Umayyah radhiallahu’anha, she said,

> **كانَ يقولُ إذا صلَّى الصُّبحَ حينَ يسلِّمُ اللَّهمَّ إنِّي أسألُكَ عِلمًا نافعًا ورزقًا طيِّبًا وعملًا متقبَّلًا**
>
> "The Prophet ﷺ used to say when he prayed Fajr, after he performed Taslim:
> **alloohumma inni as-aluka ‘ilman naafi’an, wa rizqon thoyyiban, wa ‘amalan mutaqobbalan**
> (O Allah, indeed I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and accepted deeds)."
> *(Narrated by Ibn Majah no. 762, authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Ibn Majah)*

items.title: Supplication Rabbighfirli wa Tub 'Alayya
items.description: Supplication seeking forgiveness and repentance 100x...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting supplication “Rabbighfirli wa tub ‘alayya…”

As narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad,

> **قَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ الْاَنْصَارِ اَنَّهُ سَمِعَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي صَلَاةٍ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي قَالَ شُعْبَةُ اَوْ قَالَ اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ اِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الْغَفُورُ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ‏**
>
> "A man from the Ansar said that he heard the Prophet ﷺ in his prayer saying:
> **Rabbighfirli (or: Allahummaghfirli) wa tub ‘alayya innataka antat tawwaabul ghafur**
> (O my Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance, indeed You are the One who accepts repentance, the Most Forgiving)
> 100 times."
> *(Narrated by Ahmad no. 23198, authenticated by Al-Albani in Silsilah Ash-Shahihah no. 2603)*

items.title: Supplication Allahumma A'inni 'Ala Dzikrika
items.description: The Prophet's advice to Mu'adh bin Jabal to be recited at the end of every prayer...
items.content_markdown:
### Reciting supplication “Allahumma a’inni ‘ala dzikrika…”

From Mu’adh bin Jabal radhiallahu’anhu, he said,

> **أنَّ رسولَ اللهِ صلَّى اللهُ عليهِ وسلَّمَ أخذ بيده وقال يا معاذُ واللهِ إني لَأُحبُّك واللهِ إني لَأُحبُّك فقال أوصيك يا معاذُ لا تَدَعَنَّ في دُبُرِ كلِّ صلاةٍ تقول اللهمَّ أعِنِّي على ذكرِك وشكرِك وحسنِ عبادتِك**
>
> "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took my hand and said: 'O Mu’adh, by Allah I love you, by Allah I love you.' Then he said: 'I advise you, O Mu’adh, do not leave saying at the end of every prayer:
> **Alloohumma a’inni ‘ala dzikrika wa syukrika wa husni ‘ibaadatika**
> (O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You in the best manner)."
> *(Narrated by Abu Dawud no. 1522, authenticated by Al-Albani in Sahih Abu Dawud)*
